hypothesis.hypothesis:
Define fetch_pc = redirect ? redirect_target : pc (both flops, one LUT).
Drive io_imemAddr, if_id.pc, the BHT read index (fetch_pc[7:2]) and the
pre-decode pc+imm / pc+4 adders from it. In the pc+imm adder, the pc
leg (flop -> 1 LUT) stays shorter than the imm leg
(lfsr -> is_jal decode -> imm select), so the co-critical
lfsr -> pc path gains no level.
The PC register advances from the fetched word or holds the fetch
address: CE = !stall_if || redirect;
D = (redirect && !imem_ready) ? redirect_target : next_pc.
An imem stall in the redirect cycle therefore just refetches the
target, and the D-mux select uses only early signals.
flush_id loses its redirect term (flush_id = load_use && !dmem_stall).
The word fetched in the redirect_q cycle is the correct target and
enters ID/EX normally. ex_stage still squashes the single wrong-path
entry in EX via redirect_q, unchanged.
That squashed entry's rd/ctrl are still in ID/EX during the redirect
cycle, so ID must ignore it:
  - The id_ex_w_en fed to both forward_unit instances becomes
    ctrl_q.reg_write && !redirect, an AND of two flops, off the
    rs==rd compare path. Otherwise the target would forward the
    killed entry's stale EX/MEM.alu_result.
  - hazard_unit's id_ex_mem_read input becomes
    ctrl.mem_read && !redirect, so there is no spurious load-use stall
    and stall_if in the redirect cycle can only be imem_stall.
dmem_stall and m_stall cannot occur in that cycle: EX/MEM holds the
branch/JALR (no memory op), and is_mop is already gated by redirect_q.
RVFI is unchanged: the target's pc_rdata = fetch_pc = the branch's
pc_wdata.
Effect: 1 cycle saved per redirect, ~60K of ~4.44M cycles (~1.35%),
for ~33 LUTs, no new flops, and no new logic on the EX compare/ALU
paths. Honest estimate: +1-2% fitness, below the 4.6% acceptance bar
unless place-and-route noise helps. It is proposed as the strongest
measured predictor-category lever. If it holds Fmax, it stacks with any
later Fmax work on the EX/IF paths.

title: Late-input-last tails for the three co-critical families: one ADDSUB chain + short EX result tail, precomputed redirect conditions, split high-fanout select/decode nets
motivation:
I ran `make timing TARGET=bench` on the champion (r4s1), place option 0,
92.69 MHz. The top 5 paths form THREE families, all within 0.08 ns of
each other, so fixing any one alone gains nothing.
(A) wb_data -> alu_result, 16.08 / 16.01 ns.
    - The diff (a-b) chain SUM for bit 20 arrives at 11.30 ns.
    - SIX serial LUTs of the result AND-OR follow it
      (n1384_s14/s13/s11/s6/s2/s0, 4.8 ns).
    - Via the shifter: alu_b_0 has fanout 82 (shamt), 1.9 ns route.
      Shifter LUTs reach 12.85 ns, then 4 more tail LUTs follow.
(B) b_x -> redirect_q, 16.08 ns.
    - The select flop b_x has fanout 32, 2.93 ns route.
    - Then alu_b (2 LUTs, fanout 9, 1.9 ns route) and the compare chain.
    - Then FOUR LUTs after the chain: branch_taken_s3/s1 (the
      branch_op case mux), then redirect_fire_s1/s0.
(C) lfsr -> pc, 16.01 ns.
    - imem word -> the opcode decode LUT shared with id_stage b_four/op_jal
      (fanout 27, 3.31 ns route) -> is_jal imm mux -> pred_target chain.
    - Then pred_taken (fanout 33) -> 2 LUTs -> pc D.
Roughly 55-65% of each path is routing. Each has 2-4 LUT levels or one
huge-fanout net after its latest-arriving input. The r5s0 lesson warns
that tail restructuring must use real leg arrival times, keep the final
select to <=4 inputs (one add/sub adder), and fix every co-critical
family. The r5s2 lesson says the IF family is co-critical within 0.5%.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Apply one micro-opt rule to each family: the latest-arriving signal
enters only the LAST LUT before the flop, and no late net drives more
than about 16 loads. Stages, forwarding, the predictor and cycle
behaviour are unchanged, so IPC is identical.
A. EX result (alu.sv, ex_stage.sv, id_stage.sv, core_pkg.sv)
   1. Use ONE add/sub chain:
        as = a + (b ^ {32{r_as_sub}}) + r_as_sub
      r_as_sub is registered in ID. It maps to Gowin's ALU ADDSUB mode.
      The separate diff chain and one result leg go away.
        ltu = !carry-out
        lt  = a31^b31 ? a31 : as31
      r_as_sub is set for SUB and SLT*.
   2. Give the shift amount its own 5-bit AND-OR network. It is fed by
      duplicated sh_x/sh_w/sh_r/sh_imm select flops registered in ID, and
      each shamt bit is split into 4 syn_keep copies (one per output
      byte). The fanout-82 alu_b[4:0] nets go away.
   3. Result tail:
        out = (r_as & as) | early | shift_g
      - early = logic ops | slt | (is_muldiv & m_result). Every input of
        early settles well before the chain ends.
      - shift_g = the shifter output gated by r_sll/r_shr in its last
        mux level.
      - The final LUT has <=4 inputs.
      - is_muldiv folds in as a registered leg, which removes the
        separate `is_muldiv ? m_result : alu_result` mux.
B. Redirect (ex_stage.sv, id_stage.sv, core_pkg.sv)
   1. Register in ID six one-hot "fire-on" bits: k_eq, k_ne, k_lt, k_ge,
      k_ltu, k_geu. Each already includes the polarity:
      - taken fires when pred_taken=0 and the target is aligned, which
        is imm[1]==0 since pc[1:0]=0;
      - not-taken fires when pred_taken=1.
      Also register fu (JALR, or a JAL that was not predicted).
   2. Then:
        redirect_d = ok & (fu | k_eq&eq | k_ne&!eq | k_lt&lt | k_ge&!lt
                           | k_ltu&ltu | k_geu&!ltu)
      ok = valid & !redirect_q & !stall. The eq/lt/ltu chain ends then
      see at most 2 LUTs.
   3. Duplicate the a_*/b_* select flops per byte lane (4 copies,
      syn_keep) to cut the 2.9 ns fanout-32 route.
C. IF (if_stage.sv)
   1. Give the pre-decode its own private is_jal/is_br LUTs, duplicated
      into 2-3 syn_keep copies for the imm-select mux, so it no longer
      shares the id_stage opcode LUT with its fanout-27, 3.3 ns net.
   2. Split pred_taken into syn_keep copies per PC byte to cut the
      fanout-33 route.
Expected result: each family loses about 1.5-2.5 ns on option 0,
i.e. 16.1 -> about 14.5 ns arrival, about +8-10% Fmax at the same
cycles. I discount this for placement noise and the chance that a
fourth family appears.

title: Unmuxed EX/MEM result legs with class-qualified forward selects, plus trims on the two co-critical sibling paths
motivation:
Champion r4s1: 224.29 at a median of 99.6 MHz, 4.44M cycles for 2.92M
instructions. The worst path is the EX forwarding loop, 23 cells and
12 levels (MEM/WB.wb_data -> alu_result):
  - fx/fw flop;
  - one-hot operand AND-OR (2 LUT levels);
  - adder carry chain or barrel shifter;
  - one-hot result AND-OR (2 levels);
  - is_muldiv ? m_result : alu_result (1 level);
  - EX/MEM.alu_result.
This loop is a true single-cycle loop. r5s1 moved the operand mux
across the clock edge and gained only +2.5%, because the loop closed
through the D-mux instead. So the only real cut is to remove logic
from the loop, not to move it.
The 3 levels after the ALU exist only to merge the result classes
into one 32-bit EX/MEM register. The consumer that forwards from
EX/MEM already has a one-hot AND-OR in front of it, and the
producer's result class is known in ID one cycle early (it sits in
ID/EX). So the merge can be folded into the consumer's AND-OR.
r5s2 measured three co-critical families within 0.5% on the
champion:
  - (1) this ALU loop;
  - (2) b_x select -> branch compare -> redirect_q;
  - (3) lfsr (imem data) -> pre-decode -> imm mux -> pc+imm ->
    target[20] window check -> pred_taken -> next_pc -> pc.
Lesson r5s2: cutting one family alone buys nothing. This hypothesis
therefore makes the one structural cut on (1) and adds a small,
IPC-neutral level or fanout trim to each of (2) and (3).

hypothesis.hypothesis:
A. Split EX/MEM result registers (family 1, the structural change).
   Replace EX/MEM.alu_result with four unmuxed leg registers, each
   written straight from its unit:
     - sum_q = a+b: ADD/ADDI/LUI/AUIPC/JAL/JALR link.
     - dif_q = a-b: SUB.
     - sh_q = r_sll ? shl : shr. This select merges into the last
       shifter stage.
     - lg_q = XOR/OR/AND/SLT/SLTU AND-OR, or m_result for M-ops. Both
       are shallow: 1-2 LUTs after the operands. The muldiv mux
       leaves the adder and shifter paths.
   EX/MEM also carries the producer's registered class one-hot
   (c_add, c_sub, c_sh, c_lg). mem_stage computes
     alu_result = OR(c_* & leg_q)
   before the existing mem_to_reg mux into MEM/WB.wb_data. That path
   is flop -> 2 LUTs -> flop, which is not critical.
   In ID, forward_unit's sel_x is split by the class of the ID/EX
   producer (reg_q.r_add | is_lui... -> x_add, r_sub -> x_sub,
   r_sll|r_shr -> x_sh, else -> x_lg). The registered one-hot
   selects become a_xadd/a_xsub/a_xsh/a_xlg (same for b, s1, s2).
   EX operand legs:
     - alu_a: 4 x-legs + fw + rs1 + pc = 7 AND terms.
     - alu_b: 4 x-legs + fw + rs2 + one ID-premerged constant
       register (b_const = b_four ? 4 : imm) = 7 terms.
   Imm itself stays in ID/EX for the branch target and the AGU. At
   most 8 terms keeps each operand at 2 LUT4 levels, the same as
   today.
   New loops:
     - sum_q -> AND-OR -> carry chain -> sum_q;
     - sh_q -> AND-OR -> shifter -> sh_q.
   Each is about 3 LUT levels shorter than today's 12-level loop.
   A shift or logic result feeding the next add now starts at a
   flop, not behind the result OR. IPC is unchanged: every
   forwarding case is still covered, with no new interlock.
B. Family 3 trim (IF, IPC-neutral). Use two parallel pre-decode
   adders, pc + imm_j and pc + imm_b. Both immediates are pure wiring
   from imem_data, so there is no imm-select LUT before the chains.
   A final 3:1 select (pc+4 / tgt_j / tgt_b) is driven by pred
   logic that no longer waits for the carry out.
   Drop the pred_target[20] window check from pred_taken. The IF
   target keeps only bits [19:0] (upper bits forced 0), so a
   wrong-path fetch stays inside [0, 1 MiB).
   In EX, add an early fire term: pred_taken && (branch_target[31:20]
   != 0). branch_target = in.pc + in.imm comes from ID/EX flops, so
   it is off the forwarding path. This term redirects a
   predicted-taken branch/JAL whose real target left the window, so
   pc_wdata/pc_rdata stay consistent for formal. The redirect_target_d
   select must pick branch_target in this case: today tgt_seq picks
   pc4 for every pred_taken entry. If the branch is not taken, the
   existing fire_n term still sends it to pc4.
C. Family 2 trim (fanout/levels only). Give the branch compare its
   own duplicated one-hot operand networks, cmp_a/cmp_b, with their
   own copies of the select flops. The ALU/AGU/muldiv networks'
   selects no longer also drive the compare, so each select flop
   drives ~32 loads instead of ~64-96.
   Precompute Ft = fire_u|fire_t and Fn = fire_u|fire_n (all early).
   Branch type is registered in ID as one-hot (c_eq, c_lt, c_ltu,
   c_inv), so after the compare chains
     redirect_fire = (((c_eq&eq)|(c_lt&lt)|(c_ltu&ltu)) ^ c_inv) ? Ft : Fn
   which is at most 2 LUT levels to redirect_q.
Implementation order: A first, then run `make timing` to check which
family limits; then C, then B. Keep a change only if the timing
report shows it moved its family. Record per-step Fmax in
implementation_notes. Expected: families 1-3 all drop about 1-3
levels, so the new limiter is the dmem -> load align -> wb_data path
or the LUT-RAM regfile read (~14.5-15 ns). That gives about +5-9%
Fmax at unchanged cycles (4.44M), ~+6% fitness.

lesson: - 2026-09-30 hyp-20260930-002-r6s1 (improvement, +10.26%): The EX bypass loop is a true single-cycle loop, so moving its mux across the clock edge (r5s1) or arrival-ordering and trimming it (r5s0, r6s0) gained at most +2.5%, but deleting the 3-level result merge from it did pay: EX/MEM now holds four unmuxed legs (sum, dif, sh with the sll/shr select folded into the last shifter stage, and lg for the logic/SLT result or, on M-ops, the muldiv result) plus the producer's result class, which ID already knows a cycle early; ID splits each x forward select by that class into registered one-hot leg selects, so the leg choice folds into the consumer's existing operand AND-OR (still <=8 terms, so 2 LUT4 levels, with 4/imm premerged in ID into one b_const leg), and mem_stage does the OR(class & leg) write-back merge off the critical path; this scored 247.30 vs 224.29 (~109.9 MHz implied if cycles stayed at ~4.44M, as designed but not confirmed), beating the +6% prediction; the run also bundled family-2/3 trims (private cmp_a/cmp_b compare networks, one-hot c_eq/c_lt/c_ltu ^ c_inv choosing between the premerged Ft/Fn fire terms, dual pc+imm_j/pc+imm_b IF adders, and the target[20] window check moved out of pred_taken into an EX redirect), and no per-step Fmax or timing report was recorded, so their share can't be separated; similar trims without the leg split gave no more than +2.5%, so the split is the likely driver, but the trims may still have been needed so the other co-critical families (r5s2) did not cap the gain; so to shorten a single-cycle bypass loop, move a result mux whose select is known a cycle early into the consumer's existing one-hot AND-OR, and do not just reorder it.

title: Re-port the predictor-steered 2-entry run-ahead fetch queue onto the registered-redirect champion, with dual-source ID compares so the view mux stays off the hazard/forward cones
motivation:
Direction/target prediction is used up. ISS data from r5s2 over the
timed CoreMark window (2.92M instructions, 4.44M cycles):
  - 46.3K branch mispredicts (gshare-1024 would still leave 33.5K);
  - 13.7K JALRs, all `ret`.
Each redirect costs 2 bubbles, so a perfect predictor saves only ~2.7%
of cycles. A RAS saves ~0.6%. A bigger BHT saves ~0.3%. None of these
can clear the 4.6% bar.

The largest front-end loss is still imem backpressure. About 22% of
fetch cycles stall. On every back-end stall cycle (dmem stall,
load-use bubble, MUL/DIV wait) the PC holds, and the fetched word is
thrown away and fetched again.

The predictor-steered run-ahead fetch queue banks those words. It cut
measured cycles by 6.4% twice:
  - r3s2: 4.38M -> 4.10M;
  - r4s2: 4,100,641 cycles against r3s1's ~4.38M.
Both attempts lost on Fmax. r4s2 dropped to 72.9 MHz. Its worst path
was cpu/u_id/reg_q.b_imm -> u_ex -> u_if/pc_1 (41 cells): the
*combinational* EX redirect (operand AND-OR -> branch-compare carry
chain -> redirect -> PC mux / queue control). r3s1's own worst path
was the same chain at 36 cells. The queue added ~5 cells to the
core's single worst path.

Since r4s1 (the champion) that path no longer exists. redirect_q and
redirect_tgt_q are flops. The champion's limiter is the EX forwarding
loop (wb_data -> operand AND-OR -> ALU -> alu_result, 12 levels,
~10 ns). Two other families are co-critical within 0.5%:
  - b_x -> branch compare -> redirect_q;
  - lfsr imem word -> pre-decode -> pc+imm -> pc.
A fetch queue touches none of these three when built this way:
  - The redirect only feeds a flop into the PC mux and the queue
    count/empty/full flops.
  - The pc+imm adder and the pred_taken logic are unchanged.
  - The PC clock-enable gets *simpler*. It becomes imem_ready &&
    !full_q, instead of today's stall_if. stall_if runs lfsr word ->
    load-use rs compare -> OR with dmem/m_stall -> PC CE.
So the r4s2 Fmax loss should not carry over to this base. The 6.4%
cycle saving, measured twice, should.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Decouple fetch from decode with a 2-entry predictor-steered fetch
queue. Every queue-added term hangs off registered selects or early
signals. Nothing new goes onto the EX loop, the redirect_q cone or the
pc+imm adder cone.

1. if_stage.sv: run-ahead fetch PC plus the queue.
   - `pc` becomes fetch_pc. These stay exactly as today and apply to
     the word at fetch_pc (io_imemData):
       - pre-decode (JAL / branch detect, B/J imm);
       - the pc+imm adder;
       - the agree-BHT read at fetch_pc[7:2] and the BHT write port;
       - the misalign and 1 MiB guards.
   - fetch_ok = imem_ready && !full_q, where full_q is a registered
     count == 2.
   - PC priority: reset > redirect (redirect_tgt_q) >
     fetch_ok (pred_taken ? pred_target : pc+4) > hold.
     stall_if no longer reaches the PC.
   - Queue: 2 flop entries of {pc, instr, pred_taken, pred_ctr}, as a
     shift FIFO with entry0 as the head. Registered count, full_q and
     a one-hot empty_q.
   - Decode view (if_id_t out):
       - empty_q = 1: {fetch_pc, imem_data, pred bits,
         valid = imem_ready}, with the NOP 0x13 when !imem_ready,
         as today;
       - empty_q = 0: {entry0, valid = 1}.
     Each bit is one 2:1 LUT with a registered select.
   - consume = !stall_id (new input).
   - Write rule: the fetched word enters the queue when fetch_ok and
     it is not being consumed straight through the empty_q bypass.
     Entries shift on consume.
   - redirect_q clears only count, empty_q and full_q. The entry data
     flops load on write/shift enables that never depend on redirect.
   - Remove the stall/flush inputs.
   - Invariant: pred_taken stays paired with its word in the queue,
     so the EX mispredict check and the EX/MEM BHT update are
     unchanged.

2. Keep the view mux out of the ID compare cones (new versus r4s2,
   where the rs fields went through the mux first).
   - hazard_unit: compute load-use twice, against ID/EX.rd:
       - once for the raw fetch-word rs1/rs2 (io_imemData[19:15],
         [24:20]);
       - once for entry0's rs1/rs2 (flops).
     Pick the result with the registered empty_q.
   - forward_unit: likewise, instantiate twice (fetch word and
     entry0) in id_stage and mux the six one-hot select bits by
     empty_q just before the ID/EX flops.
   - The a/b-leg and r_* opcode decode read from the view word. That
     path ends at ID/EX D-inputs and has slack.
   - Only the LUT-RAM regfile read addresses take the view mux, and
     that path (LFSR/flop -> 1 LUT -> RAM16 read -> write-first bypass
     -> ID/EX flop) is ~5 levels, far shorter than the 12-level
     EX loop.

3. hazard_unit.sv
   - Drop stall_if, flush_if and the imem_ready input.
   - Keep the stall_id / flush_id / stall_ex_mem / hold_mem_wb
     equations. flush_id = (load_use | redirect) & !dmem_stall, as now.

4. core.sv
   - Wire the view word to id_stage.
   - Wire the fetch-word and head rs fields plus empty_q to the hazard
     unit.
   - Drive consume from !stall_id.
   - The BHT update, the registered EX redirect/squash and RVFI are
     unchanged.

Expected cycle effect: 4.44M -> ~4.16M (-6.4%, the measured r3s2/r4s2
ratio; redirect penalties stay the same, since the bypass keeps
post-redirect latency at today's value). Costs ~140 FF and ~150 LUT4;
the design allows 10K LUT4.
Expected Fmax: flat within noise (~99-100 MHz). The EX loop still
sets Fmax, and the PC-CE cone gets shorter.
Net: about +6% fitness. Falsifier: if `make timing` names a
u_if-queue / consume / view-mux path as worst, the per-cone
dual-compare trick was not enough.

title: Encoded 8:1 operand muxes in EX that map onto Gowin MUX2_LUT5/6 wide-mux cells (1 LUT level, no routing hop) instead of 2-level one-hot AND-ORs
motivation:
Champion r6s1 scores 247.30 at a median of 109.9 MHz (9.10 ns). Its
logged worst path is ID/EX.pc_22 -> alu_a -> shifter -> EX/MEM.sh_0,
10 cells. The path starts with the ALU operand network. The other EX
families start with the same kind of network:
  - the ALU loops: sum_q/sh_q/lg_q -> operand -> adder/shifter/SLT
    -> leg flop;
  - the branch compare: cmp_a/cmp_b -> eq/lt chains -> Ft/Fn ->
    redirect_q;
  - the AGU: rs1 -> +imm -> mem_addr / JALR target.
Every operand network is a one-hot AND-OR with 6-8 terms:
  - 4 class-split EX/MEM x-legs;
  - MEM/WB fw;
  - the regfile value;
  - pc or b_const.
That is 12-16 LUT inputs, so each network maps to 2 LUT4 levels
with a general-routing hop between them. Earlier timing reports
measured routing at 60-70% of these EX paths (r4s1: "68% of it
routing"). So the inter-LUT hop is the expensive part of the
network, not the LUT itself.
Gowin GW2A has dedicated wide-function muxes inside each CFU
(MUX2_LUT5/6/7/8, the equivalent of Xilinx F7/F8). An 8:1 mux with a
binary 3-bit select maps to 4 LUT4s (2:1 by s0), 2 MUX2_LUT5 (s1)
and 1 MUX2_LUT6 (s2). That is one LUT level plus two ~0.1-0.2 ns
hard-mux stages on dedicated intra-CFU wires, with no general-routing
hop. A one-hot AND-OR is not a mux in structure, so synthesis cannot
use these cells and builds a 2-level LUT tree instead. r3s0's
encoded 4:1 forward mux did map to LUT4 pair + MUX2_LUT5. It lost to
r3s1's flat one-hot network only because it had a second pc/imm
operand mux in series. Here the pc/imm/const legs are already
premerged into 8 legs, so the encoded form is a single wide mux.

select code is computed and registered in ID. Registered copies of
the code bound its fanout. Cycle behaviour is unchanged by
construction: the same source is chosen in every case, only the
encoding differs.

1. Code map. Each network has exactly 8 legs:
     000 sum_q   001 dif_q   010 sh_q   011 lg_q   (EX/MEM x-legs)
     100 fw (MEM/WB.wb_data)
     101 regfile value (rs1_val / rs2_val)
     110 a: pc          | b: b_const (4 / imm / 0)
     111 a: 32'b0 (LUI) | b: b_const (spare; same as 110)
   Networks: alu_a, alu_b, rs1 (AGU base / JALR), rs2 (store data),
   cmp_a, cmp_b. The s-networks for rs1/rs2/cmp have only 6 real
   legs; their unused codes select 0 or duplicate the regfile leg.
   RVFI values stay as today.
2. ID (id_stage). Keep forward_unit's sel_x/sel_w/sel_rf priority
   unchanged. Store the ID/EX producer's result class as a
   registered 2-bit index kidx next to reg_q.k, so the x code is
   only {1'b0, kidx}. For network a:
     code = !a_rs ? (op_lui ? 111 : 110)
          : f1_x  ? {1'b0, kidx}
          : f1_w  ? 100 : 101
   b is the same, with b_rs and 110 for b_const. s1/s2/p1/p2 use
   only the x/w/r legs; cmp copies stay separate flops so they
   cannot merge with the a/b codes.
   Register four byte-lane copies of each ALU/cmp code
   (syn_keep / syn_preserve on the flops so Gowin does not merge
   them). This keeps fanout per select flop at about 32 (s0), 16
   (s1) and 8 (s2) instead of 128/64/32. rs2 (store data, off the
   critical path) may use a single copy.
3. Shift amount. Add a private 5-bit shamt network with the same
   8:1 code, from its own flop copy. The shifters' ~64 select loads
   per bit then do not sit on byte 0 of alu_b, which also feeds the
   adder, SLT and muldiv.
4. EX (ex_stage). Write each network as an indexed 8-entry leg
   array, legs[code], or as a full `case`, so GowinSynthesis infers
   MUX2_LUT5/MUX2_LUT6. Do not write it as AND-OR. Remove the
   one-hot x/w/r/pc select fields from id_ex_t. No other EX logic
   changes: ALU legs, AGU, compare, Ft/Fn fire, muldiv handshake,
   EX/MEM register and squash all stay as they are.
5. Verify the mapping before evaluation. In the Gowin netlist or
   resource report, MUX2_LUT5/MUX2_LUT6 counts should rise by about
   6 x 32 x 3. On option 1 (`python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench
   --all-options`), the ALU and compare paths should show one LUT
   plus MUX2 cells in front of the adder/shifter/compare chain
   instead of two LUTs. If synthesis flattens the case back into a
   LUT tree, write it as an explicit nested `? :` tree
   (s2 ? (s1 ? (s0 ? ..) : ..) : ..) or put syn_keep on the mux
   output. Instantiating Gowin primitives
   directly would break Verilator/cocotb, so avoid it.

at once (one routing hop plus one LUT replaced by two hard-mux
stages), about 5-9% Fmax. IPC and CRCs are unchanged, and LUT4 count
should be about flat. The family-3 IF pre-decode path is untouched;
if it becomes the limiter, the gain stops at its slack.

title: Split the barrel shifter across the EX/MEM edge (coarse byte shift in EX, fine bit shift in MEM) with a shift-use interlock
motivation:
Champion r6s1 scores 247.30: a median of 109.868 MHz (option 1 = option 2)
and 4,442,763 cycles. Its logged critical path is
cpu/u_id/reg_q.pc_22 -> cpu/u_ex/reg_q.sh_0: 10 cells, -4.05 ns slack.
The path runs from an ID/EX flop through the 2-LUT one-hot operand AND-OR
(alu_a) and the full 5-stage barrel shifter (sll and sra/srl, then the
r_sll select) into EX/MEM.sh. r6s1 took the 3-level result merge out of
the EX bypass loop, so the adder legs (sum/dif) now end at the carry
chain. The shifter is now the deepest thing left in EX: 2 operand LUT
levels plus about 5-6 shifter cells, against the adder's 2 levels plus
a fast carry chain.
The lessons show that reordering or trimming inside a stage gains at most
+2.5% (r5s0, r6s0). What paid was taking logic out of the cycle
altogether (r6s1's leg split, r4s1's registered redirect). For the
shifter, the only way to take logic out is to move part of it into the
next stage.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Split the shifter across the EX/MEM edge. Treat a shift result like a
load result: it is ready at MEM/WB, not at EX/MEM.

1. EX coarse stage (in the EX loop). From the existing alu_a/alu_b
   operand AND-ORs, do only the shamt[4:3] byte shift (0/8/16/24) for
   both directions. Right shifts use the fill bit r_sra & a[31]; left
   shifts fill with 0. Pick the direction with the ID-registered r_sll.
   Per bit, that is a 4:1 mux plus the direction select: about 2 cells,
   where the full 5-stage shifter is about 5-6.
   Register in EX/MEM:
     - the coarse word (it replaces the sh leg);
     - shamt[2:0];
     - r_sll;
     - the fill bit.
   The shamt flops can be duplicated so the fine stage is not driven by
   one high-fanout net.
2. MEM fine stage. In mem_stage, shift the coarse word by shamt[2:0]
   (0..7, left or right, with fill): an 8:1 mux per bit. The shift
   result enters the write-back merge OR(class & leg) as the last term
   before MEM/WB.wb_data, after the load / ALU select. This path is
   flop -> about 2 fine-shift cells -> 1-2 merge cells -> flop, off the
   bypass loop and shorter than the old EX shifter path.
3. Forwarding. The x-leg classes drop from 4 to 3 (sum, dif, lg), so
   each EX operand AND-OR loses one term. A shift result reaches a
   distance-2 consumer through the existing w leg
   (MEM/WB.wb_data = fw), and a distance-3+ consumer through the
   regfile, as today.
4. Shift-use interlock. Extend the hazard unit's load-use term to
   "ID/EX is a load or a shift" (a registered is_shift bit next to
   ctrl.mem_read), compared against the raw fetch-word rs1/rs2 as
   today. This puts one bubble between a shift and a consumer at
   distance 1, exactly like load-use. Every stall, flush and
   forward-select argument that already holds for loads carries over
   unchanged: a held ID/EX re-evaluates its selects and sel_x can never
   point at a shift.
5. Register-shift amount. SLL/SRL/SRA take shamt from alu_b[4:0], as
   today; immediate shifts take it from b_const.

Expected effect:
  - Fmax: the deepest EX path shrinks by about 3-4 cells. The EX critical
    path becomes the adder carry chain or the branch-compare/redirect_q
    and IF pre-decode families, which r5s2 measured as co-critical at
    the previous champion. Expect about +7..+10% Fmax, capped by those
    families.
  - IPC: the only new stall is a shift followed by a dependent
    instruction at distance 1. A static count on the -O3 coremark.elf
    (objdump; next instruction reads the shift's rd):
      - crcu16: 138 insns, 53 shifts, 22 distance-1 dependent (gcc turns
        the inlined crcu8 into bit-reverse shift/and/or ladders);
      - crcu8: 26 shifts, 9 dependent;
      - cmp_complex: 18 shifts, 7 dependent;
      - core_bench_list: 18 shifts, 7 dependent;
      - matrix_test: 30 shifts, 16 dependent;
      - core_state_transition, core_list_find, mergesort: none.
    Weighted by a rough CoreMark profile (crc about 10-15% of dynamic
    instructions), that is about 3-4% more cycles. Imem-stall bubbles
    hide part of each new bubble when a stall lands on the same cycle.
Net: about +5%, with low confidence. Break-even for the 4.6% bar needs
about +9% Fmax, so it pays only if the adder, compare/redirect and IF
families sit at least ~9% behind today's shifter path. Implementer:
time option 1 first (`python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options`)
and confirm that before polishing the rest.
Correctness: RVFI is unchanged (MEM/WB.wb_data carries the final
shift value), and formal sees one more interlock source, shaped like
load-use.

lesson: - 2026-09-30 hyp-20260930-002-r7s1 (regression, -22.85%): Splitting the barrel shifter across EX/MEM (EX does only the shamt[4:3] byte shift; MEM shifts the registered coarse word by sh_amt[2:0] in front of MEM/WB.wb_data; ID/EX is_shift joins the load-use term, so a distance-1 consumer takes one bubble) scored 190.78 vs 247.30, which implies ~85-88 MHz vs 109.9 (-20 to -23%; the low end assumes unchanged cycles, the high end the estimated +3-4% of new shift-use bubbles) instead of the +7-10% predicted, since cycles alone would need to rise ~30% to explain it, so the split must have created a new path much worse than the ~3-4 shifter cells it removed; no timing report was captured, so that path is unknown (suspects: the ex_mem_t diff shows one unduplicated sh_amt/sh_left/sh_fill set driving the whole 32-bit fine stage, although the hypothesis asked for copies, and the extra merge term behind the dmem BSRAM -> load-align -> wb_data path), and the premise was never checked on the scored option either: log.jsonl's critical_path is always option 0's path (1/(5 ns - slack) equals seeds[0] in every logged run; r6s1's pc_22 -> sh_0 path is from the 110.54 MHz option-0 run, while the median comes from option 1 at 109.87), so before paying an interlock bubble to move half of a unit into the next stage, time that split alone on option 1 (`--all-options`), and do not retry the shifter split without that report.

title: Zero-bubble `ret` via a 4-deep IF return-address stack, verified on the existing EX branch comparator
motivation:
Measured with test/cosim/reference.py on the canonical coremark.elf
(2K, -O3, 10 iterations, only the timed window between the 0x10000100 /
0x10000104 markers): 2,922,015 instructions vs 4,442,763 cycles on the
champion r6s1. Control flow is 529,588 conditional branches (294,425
taken), 49,367 JAL and 13,735 JALR, and every JALR is
`ret` (0x00008067, no indirect calls survive -O3). An offline model of
the current 64 x 2-bit pc[7:2] agree-BHT gives 46,325 branch mispredicts.
46.3K + 13.7K = ~60K redirects, which matches the +59,971 cycles that r4s1's
one extra registered-redirect bubble cost (4,382,792 -> 4,442,763), so the
model is consistent with the RTL. Each redirect costs 3 fetch slots.
Today every `ret` pays 3 slots (fire_u), because the IF predictor has no
target storage for JALR. That is ~41K cycles (0.93%) that a return
predictor can remove almost entirely. A 4-entry stack (no wrong-path
repair modelled) hits 13,723 of 13,735 returns, 2 entries 13,633, and
8 entries 13,734.
Other direction-predictor options measured in the same model are
smaller or costlier. A 256-entry agree table gives 39.6K mispredicts
(-6.7K, 0.45%). gshare with 1024 entries and 10 history bits gives 33.5K
(-12.8K, 0.87%), but it needs a history register and an XOR in front of the
table read. Smaller gshare/gselect tables are worse than the current
table. RAS is the largest single predictor lever that stays off the
late imem_data paths.
Honest ceiling: all ~60K redirects together are ~180K cycles (4.0%), so no
pure direction/target predictor on this core can clear the 4.6% bar alone.
This slot targets the cleanest ~1% and must be Fmax-neutral to be positive.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
1. IF (if_stage.sv): a 4-entry shift-register return stack of
   word-address bits [19:2] (18 bits x 4 = 72 FFs; predicted targets live
   in the 1 MiB window, like tgt_j/tgt_b). Entry 0 is always the top, so
   ras_top is a plain flop output and needs no read mux.
   - Push (shift down, entry0 <= pc+4) when pred_j && rd(imem_data[11:7]) == x1
     (JAL call; rd == x5 optional).
   - Pop (shift up) + predict when pred_r = imem_ready && is_ret, with a
     loose 2-LUT-level decode: imem_data[6:2] == 5'b11001 &&
     imem_data[11:7] == 0 && imem_data[19:15] == 5'd1. Do NOT decode the
     imm/funct3 bits here; ID validates them (step 2), so a false positive only
     costs one redirect.
   - Push/pop update exactly when the PC advances (same enable as the PC
     register: !stall && !redirect), so they stay paired with the
     instruction entering ID/EX. No wrong-path repair (wrong-path pushes
     and pops only reduce accuracy, and every predicted ret is verified in EX).
   - next_pc: merge the early legs first, early = pred_r ? {12'b0,
     ras_top, 2'b00} : pc + 4, then keep today's single final select
     pred_j ? tgt_j : pred_b ? tgt_b : early. The late tgt_j/tgt_b adder
     legs and pred_j/pred_b see the same final-LUT structure as today,
     and pred_r is as deep as pred_j.
   - if_id_t gains pred_ret and pred_tgt (the 20-bit predicted target).
2. ID (id_stage.sv): register ret_ok = pred_ret && dec_is_jalr &&
   imm == 0 && !dec_is_illegal. For ret_ok, the branch-compare operand
   selects take rs1 on p1 (p1_x/p1_w/p1_r from f1_*), set c_eq = 1 and
   c_inv = 0, and register a new constant leg p2_const = {12'b0, pred_tgt}
   (zero otherwise) with p2_x/p2_w/p2_r cleared. A pred_ret that fails
   ret_ok is marked for an unconditional redirect: to agu for a real
   JALR, or to pc+4 otherwise (e.g. an illegal word the loose IF decode
   matched), because IF already steered away from pc+4.
3. EX (ex_stage.sv): cmp_b gains the one registered leg `| p2_const`
   (7 AND terms, still 2 LUT4 levels). A ret_ok JALR is removed from fire_u
   and added to fire_n (fires only when the compare says "not equal").
   The early fire terms absorb this. The late branch_cond still only
   picks Ft vs Fn, so the compare -> redirect_q path gains no LUT level.
   The redirect target stays the existing JALR agu path (imm = 0, so agu
   == rs1). A misaligned rs1 can never match an aligned RAS entry, so it
   fires to pc4 through tgt_seq, as today. branch_taken, the BHT update
   (is_branch only), pc_next and RVFI are unchanged.
Expected cycles: -13.7K x 3 = ~-41K (-0.9%), minus a small wrong-path
pollution loss. If option-1 Fmax holds within noise, fitness rises ~1%.
The implementer should report cosim cycles and `--all-options` Fmax
separately, so the IPC gain and any IF-path cost can be credited
independently.

lesson: - 2026-09-30 hyp-20260930-003-r7s2 (regression, -14.10%): A 4-entry IF return-address stack (pop decoded loosely from the raw imem word; per the hypothesis its top merges into next_pc as `pred_r ? ras_top : pc+4` ahead of the tgt_j/tgt_b select, and push/pop share the PC enable; the ret is verified in EX by an extra constant p2_tgt leg on cmp_b, with ret_ok moved from fire_u into fire_n) was pitched as Fmax-neutral for a ~0.9% cycle saving, yet scored 212.43 vs 247.30, which implies Fmax fell from 109.9 to ~93.5-94.4 MHz (-14 to -15%; the range spans unchanged cycles and the predicted ~41K-cycle saving, neither confirmed); no timing report was captured, so the new limiter is unknown (suspects: pred_r comes from the same late imem_data as pred_j/pred_b, so the "early" pc+4 leg of next_pc is no longer early; the 72 RAS flop enables hang off the late stall/redirect PC-enable cone; both sit on the IF family r5s2 found co-critical; also the extra ret_ok/JALR terms on the cmp -> Ft/Fn -> redirect_q family); the hypothesis' own ISS data caps all ~60K redirects at ~180K cycles (~4.0%, below the 4.6% bar), and r2s2, r3s2, r4s2, r5s2, r6s2 and now this run each cost ~3.6-17% Fmax for their fetch/redirect logic, so no predictor or fetch-side IPC change can pay on this ~110 MHz core unless an option-1 (`--all-options`) timing run first shows it costs well under 1% Fmax; do not spend another slot on one without that report.

title: Take pc/b_const out of the EX alu_a/alu_b AND-ORs (3->2 LUT levels) and cut the four co-critical tails seen in the option-1 report
motivation:
An `--all-options` Gowin run on the r6s1 champion (option 1 = the scored
median, 109.868 MHz, slack -4.102 ns) shows five path families within
0.03 ns of each other. This is the first option-1 report taken on this core:
  1. ID/EX.pc_22 -> alu_a -> shifter -> EX/MEM.sh (14.396 ns). alu_a is
     THREE LUT levels (alu_a_22_s3 -> s2 -> s0) because it is a 7-leg
     AND-OR (4 class x legs + fw + rs1_val + a_pc&pc = 14 inputs). Then a
     1.2 ns route (fanout 10) into 6 shifter LUTs. rs1/rs2/cmp_a/cmp_b have
     6 legs and are only 2 levels deep.
  2. ID/EX.p1_x.sub -> cmp_a (2 LUT) -> 6-LUT compare/cond tree ->
     ctrl_with_trap.reg_write (14.395 ns). The last LUT exists only because
     misalign_branch (built from branch_taken) clears reg_write, but a
     branch never has reg_write set.
  3. muldiv b_q_3 -> res_q_16 (14.394 ns): a 6-LUT `b_q != 0` reduce feeds
     neg_quo, then the S_DFIX negate/select. Every input is a latched
     operand that has been stable for 34 cycles.
  4. p1_x.sub -> redirect_q (14.382 ns): the same compare tree plus the
     Ft/Fn pick.
  5. s1_w -> rs1 -> AGU carry -> 3:1 target mux -> redirect_tgt_q_26
     (14.364 ns, 15 cells).
The synthesis report lists no MUX2_LUT5/6 cells, so every level is a real
LUT4 plus a route hop (~0.37-0.57 ns cell + 0.2-1.2 ns net). Past lessons
say trimming one family does not pay while the others stay co-critical
(r5s0, r6s0). So this proposal trims each family named in the scored report
and adds no new cycle behaviour.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
These are IPC-neutral trims. Each removes at least one LUT level from one
of the co-critical option-1 families. None adds a level or a fanout load
to any other family.

A. alu_a / alu_b become 6-leg one-hot AND-ORs (2 LUT levels, down from 3).
   ID registers two new operand flops next to rs1_val/rs2_val:
     a_val <= a_pc ? pc : rs1_data   with select a_v = a_pc | (f1_r & a_rs)
     b_val <= b_rs ? rs2_data : b_const  with select b_v = b_rs ? f2_r : 1
   EX then computes alu_a = xleg(a_x) | a_w&fw | a_v&a_val, and alu_b the
   same way. The pc and b_const legs disappear from EX. LUI still gets
   alu_a = 0 because a_pc = 0 and a_rs = 0, so a_v = 0. JAL/JALR still get
   pc + 4. rs1_val/rs2_val stay pure for rs1/rs2/cmp_a/cmp_b/RVFI, so the
   existing regfile -> ID/EX path is unchanged. Only the new a_val/b_val
   D-inputs get the pc/const mux, and that mux can merge into the
   write-first bypass LUT. This removes one LUT level plus a route hop from
   family 1, and from the adder/SLT paths that start at alu_a.
B. The reg_write trap clear uses only misalign_jump | mem_mis.
   misalign_branch still sets is_illegal. is_illegal only reaches RVFI, so
   synthesis prunes it. This removes the compare tree from the reg_write
   endpoint (family 2). Branches have reg_write = 0 in the decoder, so the
   change is equivalent.
C. muldiv: in S_DINIT, register neg_quo_q, neg_rem_q and a sel_quo_q bit
   (DIV/DIVU vs REM/REMU). S_DFIX then computes
   res_q <= neg ? 0 - x : x, where x = sel_quo_q ? quo_q : rem_q comes
   from flops only. This removes the 6-level b_q != 0 reduce and the op_q
   decode from family 3. The ALTOPS branch is untouched.
D. JALR target taken after the edge. EX/MEM.mem_addr already registers
   the AGU sum. redirect_target_d loses its agu leg and becomes
   tgt_seq ? pc4 : branch_target, where branch_target = pc + imm is an
   early carry from flops. A new registered bit
   redirect_jalr_q = is_jalr && !agu[1] (agu[1] is an early carry bit)
   makes the output pick
     redirect_alt_q && !reg_q.branch_taken ? redirect_pc4_q
     : redirect_jalr_q ? {reg_q.mem_addr[31:1], 1'b0} : redirect_tgt_q
   This is valid because the firing JALR is the EX/MEM entry while
   redirect_q is high, and it is never dmem-stalled (no memory op). This
   takes the 32-bit AGU carry chain off the redirect_tgt_q D-input
   (family 5). The added output leg sits on a short flop -> mux -> PC path.
E. (Optional, only if cheap) compute misalign_branch's target-misalign
   term in ID (B-type imm[1] with pc[1:0] = 0) so the only late input is
   branch_cond.

After A-D, the shifter family is 2 + 6 LUTs and the compare families are
2 + 6-7 LUTs, down from 3 + 6 and 2 + 7. Expect roughly one LUT level plus
one route hop off the worst path: ~0.6-0.9 ns of 9.1 ns, i.e. +5-8% Fmax,
if the placer does not turn up a new co-critical family (the redirect_q
compare tree is the next candidate). Cycles stay at 4,442,763 by
construction.

title: Immediate-only EX shifter with a private operand network and ID-flop shamt; register shifts run in muldiv; trim the two non-shifter co-critical endpoints
motivation:
Option-1 timing of the current r6s1 champion (python3 -m tools.eval.gowin
bench --all-options, run for this hypothesis; option 1 = option 2 =
109.868 MHz, the scored median) shows a flat wall: 25 worst paths span
only -4.102 .. -3.959 ns slack (9.07 .. 8.92 ns data delay, 10 cells).
18 of the 25 end at EX/MEM.sh (the barrel shifter), starting from every
input of the shared ALU operand networks: data (ID/EX.pc_22 via the a_pc
leg, a_x.sh, MEM/WB.wb_data_14) and shamt (b_r, b_w -> alu_b[4:0], which
drives both the left and right 5-stage shifters unduplicated). The other
endpoints within 0.13 ns are: p1_x.sub -> EX/MEM.ctrl.reg_write (-4.100:
branch compare -> misalign_branch -> reg_write clear, although a branch
never writes), muldiv b_q_3 -> res_q_16 (-4.100: (b_q != 0) -> neg_quo ->
negate chain in S_DFIX), compare -> redirect_q (-4.088), JALR AGU ->
redirect_tgt_q (-4.070), SLT -> lg_0 (-4.054), pc -> redirect_pc4_q
(-4.051) and the IF path lfsr_1 -> pc_7 (-3.973).

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Give the shifter its own unit with its own inputs so it leaves the top of
the wall, and remove the two trivially-false co-critical endpoints:
(1) EX shifter handles only SLLI/SRLI/SRAI. Its shamt comes straight
from ID/EX flops loaded with fetch_word[24:20] (no logic; 4 byte-lane
copies so each copy drives <=~16 mux LUTs), and its direction/fill bits
are already ID-registered. Its data input is a private one-hot network
sh_a = xleg(sh_x) | (sh_w & fw) | (sh_r & rs1_val) with its own select
flops gated by is-imm-shift (no pc leg, not shared with the adder, AGU,
compare or muldiv loads). Shift results still forward from EX/MEM.sh at
distance 1, so no interlock and no new bubbles.
(2) Register shifts SLL/SRL/SRA (essentially absent from the timed
CoreMark loop: crc, bit_extract and calc_func all shift by constants)
are sent to the multi-cycle muldiv unit as an extra op class: operands
latched on start, one S_CALC cycle computing a_q shifted by b_q[4:0] into
res_q, result on the lg leg (k.lg), exactly like MUL's handshake. This
deletes the forwarded alu_b[4:0] -> shamt net from the EX loop entirely.
(3) ctrl.reg_write is cleared only by misalign_jump || mem_mis (branches
have reg_write=0 already; is_illegal still gets misalign_branch), taking
the compare chain off the reg_write flop.
(4) muldiv registers neg_quo / neg_rem (and b==0) in S_DINIT from a_q/b_q
so S_DFIX only negates a registered quotient/remainder.
Expected: the shifter family (72% of the top 25) moves well off the wall
and the next limiter becomes compare -> redirect_q / AGU -> redirect_tgt_q
at ~-4.07..-4.05 ns, so the measurable gain is bounded by those and by
the IF lfsr -> pc path (~1.4%) unless relieving placement congestion
around u_alu (the shifter is the largest EX block) also shortens routing
on the remaining families (~0.9 ns per cell today). IPC is unchanged
except register shifts (+2 cycles each, near-zero count). Worth running
as the data point that tells whether the flat EX wall can move at all;
the implementer must capture an --all-options timing report.

lesson: - 2026-09-30 hyp-20260930-002-r8s1 (regression, -9.09%): Giving the SLLI/SRLI/SRAI shifter a private operand network (sh_a, a 6-leg one-hot AND-OR of the four EX/MEM legs, fw and rs1_val on its own select flops) plus an ID-registered fetch_word[24:20] shamt, and sending register shifts SLL/SRL/SRA to muldiv as a one-cycle S_CALC op on the lg leg, scored 224.82 vs 247.30 (~99.9 MHz vs 109.9 if cycles stayed at ~4.44M, which they should because the timed CoreMark loop only shifts by constants; not confirmed), against +3% predicted; the bundled reg_write-clear and S_DINIT neg_quo/neg_rem trims were also in same-round r8s0, which came out flat (247.28), so the ~10% Fmax loss must come from the private shifter network, the muldiv shift path, or both; no post-change timing report was captured, so which one is unknown (suspects: sh_a adds a seventh 32-bit load on every EX/MEM leg, fw and rs1_val bit, and those nets also feed the compare -> redirect_q, AGU -> redirect_tgt_q and SLT -> lg paths that were within 0.05 ns of the worst path; the muldiv shift puts a 32-bit barrel shifter from a_q/b_q in front of the res_q D-mux, which STA times as a single-cycle path and which was already a co-critical endpoint); the likely lesson is that a private copy of an operand network does not take a unit off a flat wall fed by shared bypass sources, because it adds load to those sources, and after r7s1 (-23%) and this run (-9%) no shifter restructuring should be tried again without an option-1 (`--all-options`) timing report on that change alone.

title: Predictor/redirect paths off the EX critical wall (JALR target from EX/MEM.mem_addr, pc+4 from IF, ID-known branch misalign, no imem_ready in pred)
motivation:
Measured on the r6s1 champion with `python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench
--all-options` (option 1 = scored median, 109.868 MHz, slack -4.102 ns):
the worst 25 paths sit within 0.13 ns of each other, and five of them are
predictor/redirect logic, not ALU:
  #4  -4.100 p1_x.sub -> cmp chain -> branch_taken -> misalign_branch ->
      EX/MEM ctrl.reg_write (branches never write rd, but synthesis
      cannot know reg_write and is_branch are exclusive)
  #7  -4.088 p1_x.sub -> cmp chain -> branch_cond -> redirect_q
  #12 -4.070 / #21 -3.982 s1_w -> rs1 AND-OR -> 32-bit AGU carry ->
      JALR jump_target -> redirect_tgt_q[26]/[28] (15 cells)
  #15 -4.051 ID/EX pc -> EX pc+4 32-bit carry -> redirect_pc4_q[31]
  #23 -3.973 lfsr_1 (fetch word) -> IF pre-decode -> pc_7 (IF family,
      pred_j/pred_b also carry the lfsr-driven imem_ready)
The rest of the wall is the shifter bypass loop (sh legs) and the divider
sign-fix (b_q -> res_q). Mispredicts + JALRs are only ~5-8K/iteration
(~2-3.6% of cycles), so no direction-accuracy change can clear the 4.6%
bar, and the IF family has only 0.13 ns of slack, so no new IF predictor
structure is free (r2s2..r7s2 all lost 3.6-17% Fmax). The useful predictor
work is to make the existing prediction/redirect machinery disappear from
the timing wall, IPC-neutral by construction, so that it no longer caps the

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Four cycle-exact changes, all in the redirect/predictor cone:
1. JALR target after the edge. redirect_target_d no longer carries the
   AGU: redirect_tgt_q captures only branch_target / pc4 (ID/EX flops ->
   one pc+imm chain). Register a one-hot target select at the D side:
   rj_q = fire && is_jalr && !agu[1] (agu[1] is the 2nd carry bit, early).
   In the redirect_q cycle the JALR sits in EX/MEM and reg_q.mem_addr is
   exactly its agu, so redirect_target = rj_q ? {reg_q.mem_addr[31:1],1'b0}
   : existing (redirect_alt_q && !reg_q.branch_taken ? pc4_q : tgt_q),
   written as a flat AND-OR of registered selects (all flops; the IF PC D
   path gains at most one LUT from flops, far from the IF lfsr path).
   Removes paths #12/#21 (AGU carry -> redirect_tgt_q).
2. pc+4 from IF. IF already computes pc + 4 for next_pc; carry it through
   if_id_t / id_ex_t as pc4 and use it for redirect_pc4_q and redirect
   target selection; delete EX's own pc+4 adder (link pc+4 still goes
   through the ALU adder as today). Removes path #15.
3. Branch misalign known in ID. pc[1:0] is always 00 (every misaligned
   transfer traps to pc+4), so a taken branch is misaligned iff imm[1]
   (instr[8]). Register br_mis = is_branch && instr[8] in ID. Use it only
   for rvfi-side is_illegal/pc_next (misalign_branch = branch_taken &&
   br_mis), and compute ctrl_with_trap.reg_write from misalign_jump ||
   mem_mis only (branches have reg_write = 0 by decode). fire_t uses
   !br_mis instead of branch_target[1:0]==0. Removes path #4 and the
   branch_target low bits from the fire terms.
4. IF: drop imem_ready from pred_j / pred_b. When imem_ready = 0 the PC
   holds (stall_if) and the IF/ID entry is a valid=0 NOP (is_branch = 0,
   so fire_n / redirect_alt_q never see its pred_taken); the term is
   redundant and only drags the stall LFSR into the next_pc select cone
   (path #23 family).
Enabler (same wall, non-predictor, 3 lines): in muldiv register
neg_quo/neg_rem at S_DINIT (a_q/b_q/op_q are stable from take) so the
S_DFIX sign-fix select no longer waits on the (b_q != 0) reduction tree
(path #5).
Cycle count must stay exactly 4,442,763 (verify in cosim). Expected: the
redirect/IF/divider families drop 0.5-1.5 ns below the wall; option-1
Fmax then rests on the shifter/operand bypass loop alone, so the direct
gain is small (placement relief from ~40 fewer co-critical endpoints),
but any ALU-loop fix in the same or later rounds is no longer capped by
these families.

lesson: - 2026-09-30 hyp-20260930-003-r8s2 (regression, -3.59%): This run included all of same-round r8s0's redirect/divider trims (JALR target taken after the edge from EX/MEM.mem_addr, reg_write trap clear kept off the branch compare, muldiv sign-fix selects registered at S_DINIT), which came out flat there (247.28), yet it scored 238.43 vs 247.30 (~105.9 MHz implied if cycles stayed at 4,442,763 as designed, not confirmed; no post-change timing report was captured), so the loss most likely comes from its own additions: IF's pc+4 carried through the combinational IF->ID bundle into a new 32-bit ID/EX.pc4 to delete EX's adder (32 more loads on an adder output inside the IF next-PC family, which had only 0.13 ns slack), B/J misalign taken from imm[1], redirect_alt_q no longer gated by win_out, and imem_ready dropped from pred_j/pred_b; the run cannot say which of these is to blame, but the upside was capped from the start, because like r8s0 it left the cmp -> branch_cond -> redirect_q path (#7, 14 ps behind the worst) and the shifter bypass loop untouched, so on a flat wall an "IPC-neutral clean-up" whose best case is ~0.15% can still lose several percent, and reusing a tighter stage's adder to delete a looser stage's one adds load to the co-critical family instead of removing it.

title: Finish r8s0's wall trim: take the branch compare off redirect_q and the pc+4 adder off redirect_pc4_q
motivation:
r8s0 trimmed four of the five option-1 families on the r6s1 champion
(alu_a 7 -> 6 legs via ID-premuxed a_val/b_val, reg_write trap clear off
the branch compare, muldiv S_DFIX signs registered at S_DINIT, JALR
target taken from EX/MEM.mem_addr after the edge). It scored 247.28 vs
247.30. That is not proof the trims are useless. The one family it left
alone, p1_x.sub -> cmp_a -> compare tree -> branch_cond -> Ft/Fn ->
redirect_q (14.382 ns), was only 14 ps behind the 14.396 ns worst path,
so r8s0 was capped at about 0.15% before it ran. r8s2 left the same
family alone and also came out flat or worse.
The next endpoints in r8s1's 25-path option-1 census that nobody has
cut yet are:
  - SLT -> EX/MEM.lg_0 (-4.054 ns);
  - ID/EX.pc -> pc+4 carry -> redirect_pc4_q[31] (-4.051 ns);
  - IF lfsr_1 -> pre-decode -> pc_7 (-3.973 ns, 0.13 ns behind).
After redirect_q, the next cap is therefore about 0.05 ns deeper.
Every earlier attempt left out at least one family, so none could show
what a whole-wall trim is worth. This proposal reuses r8s0's four trims,
which already passed formal and cosim, and cuts the two EX families
those trims left alone.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Start from r8s0's four trims, applied as described in its log.jsonl
entry, and add two IPC-neutral cuts. Both keep the same cycle-by-cycle
behaviour, so the cycle count stays at 4,442,763.

(A) redirect_q: no fire-select LUT after the compare. ID registers six
per-branch "fire-on" bits, one per compare leg and outcome:
  - fe1/fe0 for eq, fl1/fl0 for lt, fu1/fu0 for ltu;
  - each bit = c_<leg> & (the fire term chosen when that leg's raw
    compare is 1 or 0, with c_inv folded in);
  - each bit is also gated by the ID-known parts of fire_u/fire_t/
    fire_n: is_branch/is_jump/is_jalr, pred_taken, and imm[1:0] for
    alignment.
In EX:
  redirect_fire = ((eq ? fe1 : fe0) | (lt ? fl1 : fl0) | (ltu ? fu1 : fu0))
                  & fire_ok_live
Three pieces of the old logic cannot be registered in ID:
  - win_out, which depends on EX's pc+imm;
  - redirect_q itself;
  - the dmem stall.
They are no longer ANDed in front of the compare. win_out goes into a
separate, early "fire_w" term: a predicted-taken branch that is out of
the window always redirects, and its target is picked after the edge
as today via redirect_alt_q and branch_taken. !redirect_q && !stall
go into the redirect_q flop's clock-enable / synchronous-clear pins,
not its D LUT. The compare stays on its own private cmp_a/cmp_b
networks. Target: at most one LUT after the eq-reduction or lt/ltu
carry chain. The goal is to cut the compare output's fanout to
redirect_q from 2 LUT levels to 1.

(B) Take the EX pc+4 carry chain off every redirect register. Today
pc4 reaches redirect_pc4_q directly and redirect_tgt_q through the
tgt_seq mux. Instead:
  - Register one flag, seq_q = tgt_seq | (pred_taken & win_out & is_branch).
    It is ID/EX-early, apart from win_out and agu[1].
  - Delete redirect_pc4_q.
  - After the edge, compute EX/MEM.pc + 4: a 30-bit incrementer on the
    EX/MEM.pc flop, a short path of about 3 ns into the PC mux. Use it
    as the redirect target when seq_q && !(alt && taken).
redirect_tgt_q then only muxes the branch/JAL target and the JALR
target (the JALR target itself is taken after the edge, as in r8s0).
The ID/EX.pc flop loses the pc+4 carry chain from its redirect loads,
and EX/MEM.pc_next (RVFI-only, pruned) can keep its own pc+4.
This is cycle-identical: the same redirects fire in the same cycles
with the same targets.

Before building, and again after the change, the implementer should run
`python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options` with a path count
large enough (>= 60) to list every endpoint within 0.45 ns of the worst
option-1 path. Then:
  - Only claim a gain if the first un-shortened family has moved at
    least ~0.4 ns.
  - If SLT -> lg_0 becomes the cap, move SLT/SLTU to the dif carry
    chain: lt = (a[31] ^ b[31]) ? a[31] : dif[31], and similarly for
    ltu from the subtractor's carry-out. That merges into lg_0 with a
    single LUT.
  - If the IF lfsr -> pc family is the cap, stop and report it rather
    than touching IF (lessons r5s2/r8s2).
Expected effect: if r8s0 was really capped only by redirect_q and the
next three families are cut too, the option-1 wall drops by about
0.3-0.5 ns (3-5%).

lesson: - 2026-09-30 hyp-20260930-001-r9s0 (regression, -1.05%): Adding to r8s0's four trims the two cuts it left out (six ID-registered per-leg fire-on bits so one LUT picks redirect_fire straight off eq/lt/ltu, with win_out in a separate fw term and !redirect_q/!stall moved onto the flop's synchronous clear; redirect_pc4_q deleted for a registered seq flag plus an EX/MEM.pc+4 incrementer and seq/alt/jalr select taken after the edge in front of IF's PC mux) scored 244.71 vs 247.30 (~108.7 MHz at the designed-unchanged 4,442,763 cycles, not confirmed, so ~95 ps worse); if the redirect_q cap had been the only thing holding r8s0 back, the worst case here would have been flat, so the new logic itself made some path longer, and no before/after `--all-options` report was recorded even though the hypothesis made one a precondition, so which path is unknown (likeliest: the post-edge pc+4/select legs added to IF's next-PC cone, whose lfsr -> pc family was only 0.13 ns behind, the same load shift that sank r8s2); "after the edge" for a redirect target means "inside the IF PC cone", and after r8s0 (flat), r8s2 (-3.6%) and this run no further IPC-neutral LUT-level trim of the ~110 MHz wall should be tried unless the implementer captures the option-1 path list before and after the change.

title: Two-tier bypass: ID pre-merges every distance>=2 operand into one flop; shifter/compare/JALR read no EX/MEM leg
motivation:
The option-1 report on the r6s1 champion (109.868 MHz, slack -4.102 ns;
quoted in r8s0/r8s1/r8s2) is a flat wall: 25 paths within 0.13 ns.
18 of the 25 end at EX/MEM.sh. They start at every input of the shared
alu_a/alu_b AND-OR: pc via a_pc, a_x.sh, MEM/WB.wb_data and b_r/b_w for
shamt. alu_a is 14 inputs, so 3 LUT4 levels, and then a 1.2 ns route
with fanout 10 into the 5-6 level barrel shifter. The rest of the wall:
- cmp_a/cmp_b (12 inputs, 2 levels) -> compare -> reg_write clear (#4)
  and -> redirect_q (#7);
- rs1 -> AGU -> JALR target -> redirect_tgt_q (#12);
- SLT -> lg_0;
- ID/EX.pc -> pc+4 -> redirect_pc4_q (pc drives 32 alu_a loads plus two
  adders);
- muldiv b_q != 0 -> neg_quo -> res_q;
- the IF lfsr -> pc family at -3.973.
Trimming one family at a time was flat (r8s0 +0.0%) or lost (r5s0, r6s0,
r8s2). Private per-unit operand copies also lost (r8s1 -9%), because each
copy added load to the shared bypass nets.
The structural cause: every EX operand network merges all its sources in
EX: 4 EX/MEM class legs, MEM/WB.wb_data, the regfile flop, pc and const.
Of these, only the four EX/MEM legs are truly single-cycle loop inputs.
The distance>=2 value is already known one cycle earlier: it is
mem_stage's wb_data D-input while the consumer is in ID. The regfile, pc
and const are also ID-side values.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move to a two-tier bypass so every EX operand network loses at least one
LUT level, and the slowest units (shifter, branch compare, JALR target)
lose their whole EX operand network.

1. Pre-merged operand flop (ID/EX), one per network: pa, pb, ps1, ps2.
   These replace rs1_val/rs2_val/pc/b_const and the w legs as EX sources.
   D-input = one-hot AND-OR in ID of:
     - mem_wb_d: the new wb_data D-input from mem_stage, exported. It is
       the distance-2 producer's merged result, or its aligned load data.
     - regfile rs1_data/rs2_data: write-first, covers distance 3.
     - pc (a side), and 4/imm (b side).
   The flop is forced to 0 when the ID-side sel_x (distance-1) is set,
   so EX ORs it in with no select bit.
   This is exact under the same argument as forward_unit: ID/EX captures
   only when ID/EX, EX/MEM and MEM/WB advance together. dmem_ready is
   therefore 1 whenever a distance-2 load's data is captured.
   The fw (MEM/WB.wb_data) leg and the s*_w/*_r/a_pc select flops go
   away. MEM/WB.wb_data then only feeds the regfile write port and the
   write-first bypass.

2. EX operand networks become (4 class-split x legs) | pre. That is 9
   inputs, always 2 LUT4 levels. alu_a was 3 levels, so it drops one.
   rs1/rs2 lose 2 legs, and fanout drops on pc and wb_data.

3. The shifter reads ONLY the pa flop: data = pa, shamt = pb[4:0].
   There is no x leg and no AND-OR, so the shifter family drops by
   3 LUT levels and the 1.2 ns fanout route.
   The branch compare reads (p_sum & EX/MEM.sum) | pre: one x leg, which
   is 3 inputs and 1 LUT level. It keeps its own select flops.
   JALR reads ps1 only, through a private ps1+imm adder into
   redirect_tgt_q (flop -> carry -> 1 LUT -> flop).
   When an instruction needs a distance-1 value that these restricted
   readers cannot take, it waits one cycle in EX. That covers:
     - a shift/SLL/SRL/SRA with f1_x (or f2_x for register shifts);
     - a branch whose distance-1 producer is not the add class;
     - a JALR with f1_x.
   The wait uses the m_stall mechanism: ID registers a need_wait bit,
   EX raises x_stall once, PC and ID/EX hold, and EX/MEM takes a bubble.
   During that cycle the waiting entry's pre flops reload from mem_wb_d.
   The fetch word is never decoded for this, so the IF/PC-enable cone
   gains no LUT level; x_stall just joins m_stall.

4. Wall clean-ups that go with the new structure:
   - Drop misalign_branch from the reg_write clear. A branch never has
     reg_write set; is_illegal still sees it.
   - Register neg_quo/neg_rem (and b_q != 0) at S_DINIT.
   - redirect_pc4_q comes from an ID-registered pc4 flop, computed in ID
     from the pc flop with its own adder. Do NOT reuse the IF next_pc
     adder (r8s2 lesson).

Expected cycle cost: a bubble for each distance-1 non-add -> branch,
distance-1 -> shift and distance-1 -> JALR pair. In CoreMark -O3 the
shifts are by constants; their inputs are mostly loads (already
interlocked) or xor/and results. Estimated +1.5-3% cycles (the
implementer must measure the count in cosim, and report
cycles vs 4,442,763).
Expected Fmax: the shifter family (18/25 paths) loses about 3 cells. The
compare/redirect families lose 1 operand level. alu_a loses 1 level.
JALR/pc4/muldiv/reg_write each lose most of their EX depth.
The IF family (-3.973) then becomes the cap, about 1.5% above the old

Export the combinational wb_data (mem_wb_d) as an output so ID can pre-merge distance-2 values. MEM/WB register unchanged.

Wire mem_wb_d from mem_stage to id_stage. Remove fwd_mem_wb into EX. Pass the new interlock inputs to hazard_unit.

lesson: - 2026-09-30 hyp-20260930-002-r9s1 (regression, -0.76%): The two-tier bypass (ID pre-merges every distance>=2 source, i.e. mem_stage's wb_data D-input, the write-first regfile read, pc and 4/imm, into one pa/pb/ps1/ps2 flop per operand network that EX simply ORs with the four class-split EX/MEM legs; the shifter reads only pa/pb[4:0], the branch compare takes only the EX/MEM sum leg, JALR reads only ps1, and every other distance-1 use by those units waits one cycle through an x_stall ORed into m_stall) scored 245.41 vs 247.30; no cycle count, Fmax or timing report was recorded, but the change can only add cycles, so Fmax cannot be below ~109.0 MHz, which means no new path (including r5s1's suspect, load data -> mem_wb_d -> ID pre-merge flop) is more than ~0.8% slower than the old wall; the loss was already in the hypothesis' own numbers: the untouched IF lfsr -> pc family (-3.973 ns) caps any EX-side gain at ~111.4 MHz (+1.44%), while the new waits were estimated at +1.5-3% cycles, and the score fits Fmax reaching exactly that cap with ~2.2% more cycles (inferred, not measured); so before trading interlock bubbles for Fmax, check that the cycle cost is below the gap to the first co-critical family the change leaves untouched, and on this core the IF next-PC family must come off the wall before the two-tier bypass (a structure that looks Fmax-safe) or any other bubble-for-Fmax trade can pay.

title: Registered branch outcome: pick the Ft/Fn redirect fire after the edge, and take imem_ready off IF pre-decode
motivation:
Option-1 report on the r6s1 champion (109.868 MHz, from r8s2's
`--all-options` run): the worst 25 paths sit within 0.13 ns, and the
predictor/redirect machinery owns several of them:
  #4  -4.100 p1_x.sub -> cmp_a -> compare tree -> branch_taken ->
      misalign_branch -> EX/MEM.ctrl.reg_write
  #7  -4.088 p1_x.sub -> cmp_a -> compare tree -> branch_cond -> Ft/Fn
      pick -> redirect_q
  #12/#21 JALR AGU carry -> redirect_tgt_q
  #15 ID/EX.pc -> pc+4 carry -> redirect_pc4_q
  #23 -3.973 lfsr (fetch word) -> IF pre-decode (pred_j/pred_b, which
      also AND in imem_ready) -> pc
r8s0 trimmed families 1/2/3/5 and came out flat (247.28) because #7 was
left 14 ps behind the worst path. r8s2 also left #7 and added loads to
the IF family and lost 3.6%. No direction or target predictor can clear
the 4.6% bar on IPC alone (all ~60K redirects cost ~2.7% of cycles), and
every new IF structure so far cost 3.6-17% Fmax. So the most useful
predictor work in this slot is to take the redirect decision out of
the EX single-cycle compare path with zero cycle cost, and to cut one
input from the IF pre-decode, without adding any load to the shared
bypass nets.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Keep cycle behaviour identical (the 4,442,763-cycle trace must not
change) and remove the last LUT level from each predictor/redirect
family on the wall.

1. Registered branch outcome (ex_stage.sv). Today redirect_q is loaded
   with `branch_cond ? fire_tt : fire_nn`. The late branch_cond passes
   through one more LUT, and then a flop. Instead register three flops:
     cond_q  <= branch_cond   (only when the EX/MEM register advances)
     ft_q    <= fire_tt
     fn_q    <= fire_nn
   and define redirect = cond_q ? ft_q : fn_q (a single LUT3 after
   flops). The existing fire_ok gating (!redirect, !stall) stays inside
   ft_q/fn_q, so redirect has exactly the same value each cycle as
   today's redirect_q. The compare path now ends at cond_q, one LUT
   level shorter (#7). The redirect consumers (PC D-mux/CE,
   flush_id, EX kill, is_mop gate, fire_ok of the next entry) are
   flop -> 1 LUT -> fanout paths, far off the wall. Duplicate cond_q/
   ft_q/fn_q (2-3 syn_keep copies) so the consumer fanout does not
   add a slow route. Also derive redirect_target's alt pick from the
   same flops as today (redirect_alt_q && !reg_q.branch_taken).
2. reg_write trap clear without the compare (ex_stage.sv, family #4).
   Clear ctrl.reg_write only on misalign_jump | mem_mis. Keep
   misalign_branch setting is_illegal (RVFI-only). Branches never have
   reg_write set, so this is exactly equivalent. This is the same trim
   as r8s0 B, which passed formal and cosim.
3. JALR target and pc+4 after the edge (ex_stage.sv, #12/#21/#15). The
   firing JAL/JALR/branch sits in EX/MEM while redirect is high, and
   is never dmem-stalled. So redirect_target picks
     alt  ? EX/MEM.pc + 4 (computed from the EX/MEM.pc flop)
     jalr ? {EX/MEM.mem_addr[31:1], 1'b0}
          : redirect_tgt_q (branch/JAL pc+imm, or pc+4 for tgt_seq)
   with alt/jalr as registered bits. This takes the AGU carry and the
   EX pc+4 carry off the redirect_tgt_q / redirect_pc4_q D-inputs
   (r8s0 D, plus the pc+4 version). Do NOT move pc+4 into ID/IF: r8s2's
   IF-side pc+4 lost 3.6%.
4. IF pre-decode drops imem_ready (if_stage.sv, #23). When
   imem_ready=0, stall_if already holds the PC and flush_if makes the
   ID/EX entry a valid=0 bubble. So next_pc and pred_taken are
   don't-care on those cycles, and pred_j/pred_b lose one input
   (imem_ready is the lfsr-driven bus flop). The predicted target is
   still truncated to 20 bits, so wrong-path fetch stays in the window.
   Add no other logic to IF.
5. alu_a/alu_b to 2 LUT levels (id_stage.sv/ex_stage.sv, family 1 of
   the shifter loop). This is r8s0 A: ID registers a_val = a_pc ? pc :
   rs1_data and b_val = b_rs ? rs2_data : b_const next to rs1_val/
   rs2_val, so the pc and b_const legs leave the EX AND-OR. This adds
   no load to the EX/MEM legs or fw. rs1_val/rs2_val stay pure.
Items 2, 3 and 5 are known-equivalent from r8s0 (it passed all gates).
Items 1 and 4 are new and are cycle-exact by construction.

Expected: the worst path drops by about one LUT plus a route hop on
every predictor/redirect family and on the alu_a family. The remaining
families are the shifter-loop legs (2 + 6 LUT after item 5) and the
divider sign-fix (keep r8s0 C if it is cheap: register neg_quo/neg_rem
/sel_quo at S_DINIT). Honest ceiling: the wall is 25 paths wide, so the
gain is whatever the first untrimmed path's gap turns out to be.
Estimated +2-5% Fmax at unchanged cycles. The implementer must report
cosim cycles (must equal 4,442,763) and the option-1 worst-10 path list
(`python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options --paths 30`) so the
next slot knows which family is left.

lesson: - 2026-09-30 hyp-20260930-003-r9s2 (regression, -4.78%): Registering the branch outcome next to both fire terms (three syn_keep copies each of cond_q/ft_q/fn_q, with redirect = cond_q ? ft_q : fn_q picked after the edge), added to r9s0's post-edge target select (EX/MEM.pc+4 incrementer, EX/MEM.mem_addr JALR leg, registered alt/jalr bits), r8s2's removal of imem_ready from pred_j/pred_b and r8s0's flat alu_a/reg_write trims, scored 235.47 vs 247.30, which implies ~104.6 MHz at the designed-unchanged 4,442,763 cycles (~0.46 ns worse than 109.87; not confirmed, since the implementer left no notes, cycle count or path list although the hypothesis required them); the "flop -> 1 LUT -> fanout, far off the wall" premise ignored that the redirect's main sinks are the IF PC CE and D-mux, whose last LUTs are shared with the late lfsr -> pre-decode -> pc family (0.13 ns behind), so each select bit and data leg moved past the flop likely gives the mapper more inputs to fold into that late path; the three runs that moved redirect logic past the edge lost more as more of it landed in front of the PC mux (r8s0 JALR leg only, flat; r9s0 plus pc+4 and the 3-way select, -1.05%; this run plus the redirect bit itself, -4.78%), and the imem_ready removal is the only change shared by the two biggest losses (r8s2 -3.6%, this run), so it is also a suspect; keep redirect_q and redirect_tgt_q as pure flops feeding the PC mux directly, shorten the compare -> redirect_q path only on the flop's D side (in ID or in the fire terms), and do not retime redirect logic past that flop again.

title: Flop-side-only wall trim: premerged alu_a/b, per-leg redirect fire bits, late-leg-last IF next-PC and redirect target
motivation:
The r6s1 champion (247.30, 109.868 MHz on option 1, 4,442,763 cycles)
sits on a flat option-1 wall. The EX families are all within 0.03 ns:
alu_a (7 legs, 3 LUT levels) -> shifter -> EX/MEM.sh; cmp -> compare
tree -> reg_write clear; muldiv b_q != 0 -> res_q; cmp -> Ft/Fn ->
redirect_q; rs1 -> AGU -> 3:1 target mux -> redirect_tgt_q. The IF
lfsr -> pre-decode -> next_pc -> pc family is 0.13 ns behind.
r8s0 cut four of the EX families and came out flat, because
cmp -> redirect_q was left 14 ps behind the worst path. r9s0 and r9s2
also cut redirect_q, but they did it by moving redirect logic past the
flop, which puts it in front of IF's PC mux, and they lost 1-5%.
No run so far has cut every EX family on the flop's D side only and
also shortened the IF family without adding a load to it.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
IPC-neutral by construction (cycles must stay 4,442,763). Every change
is on a D input and removes a LUT level or moves a late input to the
last LUT. Nothing moves past a flop, and no net on the IF next-PC or
PC-enable cone gets a new load.
A. alu_a/alu_b become 6-leg AND-ORs (r8s0 A, flat on its own but
   needed): ID registers a_val = a_pc ? pc : rs1_data and
   b_val = b_rs ? rs2_data : b_const, with selects a_v/b_v. rs1_val and
   rs2_val stay pure for rs1/rs2/cmp and RVFI.
B. The reg_write trap clear uses only misalign_jump | mem_mis
   (branches never write rd); is_illegal still takes misalign_branch.
C. muldiv (real branch only): register neg_quo_q, neg_rem_q and
   sel_quo_q at S_DINIT, so S_DFIX is flop -> negate -> res_q. ALTOPS
   is untouched.
D. redirect_q D side: ID registers six fire-on bits (fire if eq, if
   !eq, if lt, if !lt, if ltu, if !ltu), built from c_* and the
   early fire_u/fire_t/fire_n terms of the entry's own prediction
   bits. EX then computes redirect_fire as one AND-OR of the compare
   outputs with those bits, plus the early JALR/unpredicted-JAL/win_out
   term. Gate !redirect_q && !stall through the flop's sync clear /
   CE, not the D LUT. redirect_q and redirect_tgt_q stay pure flops
   that feed the PC mux directly (r9s2 lesson).
E. redirect_tgt_q D side: precompute other = seq ? pc4 : branch_target
   (all early) and jsel = is_jalr && !agu[1], so the late upper AGU
   bits enter only the last LUT: tgt_d = jsel ? {agu[31:1],0} : other.
F. IF next-PC, from a fresh option-1 report (path 23, 14.268 ns,
   0.128 ns behind): lfsr_1 -> u_id/u_decoder -> u_id -> u_if ->
   pc_7. IF's is_jal/is_br pre-decode has been merged with the ID
   decoder's opcode LUTs, which also drive ctrl_q, imm_gen and the
   select flops, so the IF select waits on a high-fanout decoder net.
   Give IF a private pre-decode: is_jal/is_br/pred_j/pred_b computed
   from the raw imem_data bits under (* syn_keep *) so they cannot be
   shared with the decoder, and have nothing but next_pc and the
   pred_taken flop read them. Also reorder the select so the late
   inputs enter only the last LUT: pre = pred_j ? tgt_j : pc+4,
   next_pc = pred_b ? tgt_b : pre (pred_j and pred_b are mutually
   exclusive by opcode). Keep imem_ready in pred_j/pred_b (removing it
   was in both of the biggest recent losses). IF gets no new signal.
G. redirect_pc4_q (path 15, 0.05 ns behind): pc_4 -> 30-bit
   incrementer -> redirect_pc4_q_31. Step A removes the ID/EX.pc
   flop's 32 alu_a loads, which should shorten this path as well. Do
   NOT take pc+4 from IF (r8s2 lesson).
The implementer must run
`python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options --paths 40` before and
after, report the option-1 path lists in implementation_notes, and drop
any step whose family did not move. Expected: the EX wall loses one LUT
level plus a route hop (~0.5-0.8 ns), and the gain is capped by the
first family left untouched. If IF moves by at least 0.3 ns, that is
about +4-6% Fmax.

Register a_val/b_val and a_v/b_v. Register the fire-on bits from the decoded branch type, pred_taken and the B-imm misalign bit; everything that depends on EX-time state (win_out, redirect_q, stall) stays in EX as a separate early term.

title: Registered fetch stage: a 2-entry fetch buffer that ID always reads, with no raw-word bypass
motivation:
The r6s1 champion runs at 109.87 MHz and 4,442,763 cycles. Its option-1 wall is flat:
25 paths within 0.13 ns, mostly the EX shifter/compare/AGU families. Nine rounds of
IPC-neutral EX trims gave at best 0% (r8s0, r9s0, r9s1, r9s2), so a win has to come from
cycles. The largest cycle bucket not yet claimed is imem stalls (~22% of fetch slots).
Three fetch queues each measured ~6.4% fewer cycles (r3s2, r6s2 inferred, r4s2), but lost
3.5-17% Fmax. All three used the same design: ID's view was
`empty_q ? raw imem word : queue head`. That view mux sat in front of the LUT-RAM
regfile address, the decoder, the forward-select compares and the load-use compare, so
every ID-side path got one more LUT level plus a heavily loaded select net. r6s2 also
duplicated the compares. The view mux itself was the cost; buffering was not.
Today the raw fetch word (the lfsr flop in the timed wrapper) has a huge fanout: IF
pre-decode, decoder, imm_gen, regfile read addresses, both forward units and the load-use
compare. Through stall_if, the load-use compare also drives the PC clock enable. That is
why the IF family (lfsr -> pc, -3.973 ns) sits only 0.13 ns behind the wall.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make fetch a real pipeline stage. ID reads ONLY a registered buffer head. There is no
raw-word bypass and no view mux, so every ID input is a local low-fanout flop.
1. Fetch buffer (new rtl/fetch_buf.sv, or in if_stage.sv). It has 2 entries of
   {instr, pc, pred_taken, pred_ctr, valid}. The head (entry 0) is a dedicated flop set that
   ID reads directly. Entry 1 is the skid slot. Count flags live in their own flops:
   hv_q = head valid, sv_q = skid valid.
   - Write: the IF-stage word is valid when imem_ready and not killed. It goes to the head
     if the head is empty or is consumed this cycle (and skid is empty); otherwise it goes
     to the skid.
   - Consume: consume = hv_q && !stall_id. On consume, head <= skid if sv_q, else the new
     word, else invalid.
   - Build the head/skid D-muxes as one-hot AND-ORs on registered flags plus !stall_id.
     stall_id comes from flops: registered load-use from the head, dmem_stall, m_stall.
2. PC enable: `fetch_en = imem_ready && !(sv_q && hv_q && !consume_early)`. The simplest
   safe form is `imem_ready && !sv_q`, which fetches only while the skid is free. The PC
   CE loses the lfsr -> load-use compare -> stall_if path and the dmem/m_stall terms.
   Redirect still wins: redirect_q loads redirect_tgt_q and clears hv_q/sv_q (flop sync
   clears, no data muxing).
3. Keep the zero-bubble predictor exactly as it is: pre-decode, BHT, and pc+imm_j/pc+imm_b
   on the raw word steering next_pc. Do not add to it. Now only the predictor, the two
   buffer slots and the RVFI/instr copy load the raw word. pred_taken/pred_ctr travel with
   the entry.
4. ID reads the head flop: decoder, imm_gen, regfile addresses, forward_unit rs fields,
   and the ID-registered operand/select logic. The load-use compare in hazard_unit uses
   head.instr[19:15]/[24:20] against ID/EX.rd. From ID/EX onward the pipeline is
   unchanged: operand networks, class-split legs, registered redirect, squash in EX, and
   flush_id on redirect_q (now it also clears the head). The forward-select one-cycle-early
   argument still holds, because ID/EX captures on the same conditions as before.
Cycle model:
- The buffer banks words on dmem-stall, load-use and M-op cycles. It hides imem stalls
  that follow, which was the ~6.4% measured three times.
- Every redirect pays one extra refill cycle (fetch -> head -> ID/EX). ~60K redirects
  give about +1.35%.
- Net about -5% cycles.
Fmax model: the EX wall is unchanged. The IF family loses its load-use/stall CE inputs and
most of the raw-word fanout. ID paths start at a local flop instead of the high-fanout
lfsr. Expect Fmax flat to +1%, so the net is about +5-6%.
Implementer preconditions:
- Run `python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options --paths 25` before and after, and
  record the option-1 top 25 and the cosim cycle count vs 4,442,763 in
  implementation_notes.
- If the option-1 Fmax is more than 1.5% below 109.87 MHz, report the new limiter paths.
  Do not stack trims on top.
