lesson: - 2026-09-30 hyp-20260930-002-r10s1 (regression, -8.16%): A registered fetch stage (2-entry head+skid fetch_buf; decoder, regfile addresses, forward units and load-use read only the head flops, with no raw-word bypass or view mux; PC CE = imem_ready && room from registered flags) matched its cycle model exactly (4,220,319 vs 4,442,763 cycles, -5.01%: the known ~6.4% imem-stall hiding minus one refill cycle per redirect), but option-1 Fmax fell to 95.85 MHz (-12.8%), and the implementer's top 25 paths contain no IF or buffer path, only the unchanged EX wall (shifter, compare -> redirect_q, redirect_tgt_q, lg) at ~15.7 ns vs 14.40 ns before, so the r3s2/r4s2/r6s2 theory that "the view mux was the cost" is refuted: fetch buffering here costs Fmax by disturbing how the congested EX wall is placed and mapped, not through its own logic; the one extra term also mattered, because a registered head that is empty (valid=0) still holds a stale word whose decoded reg_write/mem_write reached ID/EX and broke forwarding (formal reg_ch0 failed, cosim hung), a case the old IF NOP mux had covered for free, and the build before the ID/EX ctrl-zero fix was at 103.9 MHz at option 1 (-5.4%, although functionally wrong), so fixing it cost roughly another 8%; after four fetch-buffer variants each lost 3.5-17% Fmax, do not buffer fetch again in any form (bypassed or registered) unless the EX wall first has real slack, and treat any new ID/EX D-side term as able to move that wall by several percent.

title: Predictor-steered fetch decoupled from backend stalls: PC CE = imem_ready & !full_q, 2-entry fetch buffer, stall compares kept off the PC
motivation:
Measured on the r6s1 champion (reference.py, timed window): 2,922,015
instructions in 4,442,763 cycles (CPI 1.52). All ~60K redirects
(46.3K branch mispredicts + 13.7K ret) cost ~180K cycles (4.0%), so no
pure direction/target predictor (RAS 0.93%, gshare-1K 0.87%, 256-entry
agree 0.45%) can clear the 4.6% bar; r7s2 (RAS in the IF next-PC mux)
lost 14% Fmax for 0.9%.
The only predictor-side lever above the bar is letting the
predictor-steered fetch run ahead of the backend: when ID/EX cannot
accept (dmem stall, load-use, MUL/DIV stall) the fetched word is
discarded today and must be re-fetched with another 22% imem-stall
chance. A 2-entry buffer banked those words and cut cycles by ~6.4%
twice (r3s2: 4.38M -> 4.10M; r6s2: 4.44M -> 4.16M, measured cycles),
but cost ~3.5-3.7% Fmax each time because the buffer's view mux and
its consume enable sat on late nets.
On the r6s1 option-1 report the IF family is "lfsr -> pre-decode ->
pc+imm -> next_pc -> pc" at -3.973 ns (0.13 ns under the -4.10 wall).
Today the PC clock-enable additionally hangs off stall_if =
load_use(lfsr rs fields vs ID/EX.rd) | dmem_stall | m_stall, i.e. a
second lfsr-sourced cone into the same 32 PC flops. Decoupling fetch
deletes that cone from the PC: the PC enable becomes
(imem_ready && !full_q) — one registered bit and one input — so the IF
family can only get shorter, and the consume-side logic is kept away
from both the PC and the EX wall.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Build a 2-entry fetch buffer between the predictor-steered IF and ID,
with every buffer control either a flop or a single-LUT function of
flops, and with no buffer signal reaching the PC D-mux or any EX-stage
network.
1. Fill side (if_stage). pc advances when imem_ready && !full_q
   (redirect still overrides and loads redirect_target). The IF
   pre-decode / BHT / pc+imm adders stay exactly as today on the RAW
   imem word (prediction is made at fetch time and stored with the
   entry: pc, instr, pred_taken, pred_ctr). stall_if from hazard_unit
   no longer touches the PC. A fetched word goes into the buffer when
   imem_ready && !full_q && !(buffer empty && ID consumes it directly).
2. Buffer: two entries e0 (head) / e1, count flops empty_q / full_q.
   Entry enables are functions of (imem_ready, consume, empty_q,
   full_q) only. redirect clears empty_q/full_q only (not the data).
3. Consume side (ID). The decode view is
     view = empty_q ? {imem pc, imem word, imem pred} : e0.
   To keep the view mux off the LUT-RAM regfile address and the
   forward/load-use compares, compute rs1/rs2 regfile reads, the two
   forward_unit compares and the load-use compare TWICE (once on the
   raw imem word, once on e0's registered rs fields: e0's copies are
   flop-sourced, so they are early) and pick with the registered
   empty_q after the compare (1 LUT on a 1-bit result). The regfile
   gets a second read-port pair (duplicate LUT-RAM, same write port)
   for e0's addresses, so no address mux either; ID/EX rs1_val/rs2_val
   take empty_q ? raw_read : e0_read.
   consume = !stall_id (unchanged meaning); a bubble enters ID/EX when
   empty_q && !imem_ready (was flush_if).
4. hazard_unit: stall_if output removed (or left unconnected); the
   load-use compare uses the empty_q-selected compare result;
   flush_id / stall_id / stall_ex_mem / hold_mem_wb unchanged.
5. Redirect: redirect_q / redirect_tgt_q stay pure flops feeding the
   PC mux directly (lesson r9s2); on redirect the buffer empties
   (empty_q <= 1, full_q <= 0) and flush_id still kills ID/EX, so
   wrong-path entries never retire.
Expected: cycles 4.44M -> ~4.16M (-6.3%, the r6s2 measurement). Fmax:
the PC enable loses the lfsr -> load-use -> stall_if cone, the view
mux reaches only ID/EX D-inputs (ID-side paths are not on the
option-1 wall list), and the EX networks are untouched, so the cost
must stay below ~1.5% for a net of >= +4.7%.
Precondition for the implementer: capture `python3 -m tools.eval.gowin
bench --all-options` on the unmodified core and on the change, and
record the option-1 worst path and the first path ending in the
buffer / ID/EX / PC flops in implementation_notes.md, so the result can
be attributed either way.

lesson: - 2026-09-30 hyp-20260930-003-r10s2 (regression, -16.91%): A bypassed 2-entry fetch buffer rebuilt so no buffer signal touched the PC and no view mux sat in front of an address or compare (PC CE = imem_ready && !full_q with stall_if deleted; a second LUT-RAM regfile read-port pair plus doubled forward and load-use compares for e0's registered rs fields, with the registered empty_q picking the result after the compare) scored 205.48 vs 247.30, which implies ~85.5-91.3 MHz vs 109.9 (-17 to -22%; the range spans the predicted 4.16M and the unchanged 4.44M cycles, and the implementer left no notes, cycle count or path list although the hypothesis required them), against the <=1.5% predicted and about twice the loss of same-round r10s1's registered buffer with no bypass (-8.16%, 95.8 MHz); so removing the lfsr -> load-use -> stall_if cone from the PC enable bought nothing, and duplicating the regfile read ports and compare networks to keep a 1-LUT view mux off late nets cost far more than the mux had cost on r6s2 (~3.7%, inferred), which fits r10s1's finding that fetch buffering costs Fmax through added area and load near the congested EX wall (here also extra fanout on the regfile write-data and forward-rd nets) rather than through its own logic depth; on this ~110 MHz core never duplicate a LUT-RAM read port or a compare network to take a mux off a path, and treat r10s1's "no more fetch buffers" rule as confirmed by a fifth variant.

title: One-stall MUL: product read combinationally from the DSP input registers, done raised in S_CALC
motivation:
Every IPC-neutral LUT-level trim of the ~110 MHz EX wall since r6s1 has
come out flat or negative (r8s0 -0.01%, r8s2 -3.6%, r9s0 -1.05%, r9s2
-4.8%, r10s0 -1.6%). The wall is five co-critical families within
0.03 ns, and the IF lfsr -> pc family is only 0.13 ns behind, so any
single-family Fmax trim is capped at about +1.4%. Every fetch-side IPC
change (fetch queues, RAS, earlier redirect fetch) cost 3.5-17% Fmax.
One IPC lever that sits entirely off both the fetch cone and the EX
bypass loop is still unused: the M-unit. Each MUL/MULH* stalls in EX for
2 extra cycles (start cycle, S_CALC cycle, then done_q is visible on the
third cycle) although its operands are already latched in a_q/b_q after
the first cycle. CoreMark's matrix kernel (matrix_mul_const,
matrix_mul_vect, matrix_mul_matrix, matrix_mul_matrix_bitextract, run
from calc_func for every uncached list element) issues one MUL per
multiply-accumulate, so MULs are a steady per-iteration cost, not a
one-off.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Cut the MUL stall from 2 cycles to 1 without adding logic to any path on
the current wall:
  - muldiv: drop the prod_q register. a_q/b_q plus the a_sx_q/b_sx_q
    extension bits become the DSP's input registers (they only load on
    `take`), and the 33x33 signed product is read combinationally from
    them. The hi/lo select (prod_hi_q, registered) stays after the DSP.
  - done: raise it in S_CALC for multiplies (done = done_q ||
    (state_q == S_CALC && is_mul_q)), both from flops. If ack arrives in
    S_CALC (EX/MEM not dmem-stalled), go straight to S_IDLE; otherwise go
    to S_DONE as now. The product stays valid in S_DONE because a_q/b_q
    only change on `take`, and take needs S_IDLE.

title: Resolve branches in MEM on registered operands: delete the EX compare networks and give load->branch pairs zero bubbles
motivation:
The r6s1 champion (247.30, ~109.9 MHz, 4,442,763 cycles for 2,922,015
instructions) has a flat EX wall. Two of its families exist only because
the branch compare sits in EX: cmp_a/cmp_b (private 8-leg operand AND-ORs
that add 2 loads to every EX/MEM leg bit, fw bit and rs_val bit) ->
32-bit compare -> Ft/Fn -> redirect_q, and rs1 -> AGU -> JALR target ->
redirect_tgt_q. Yet the redirect only acts one cycle later, when the
branch already sits in EX/MEM (the registered-redirect design). So the
compare can run in MEM on registered operands and drive the same
redirect in the same cycle, with no change to the 2-bubble penalty.
Moving it also removes a cycle cost. A branch that uses a load at
distance 1 currently takes the load-use bubble. When branches compare in
MEM, that load is already in MEM/WB, so the compare can read
MEM/WB.wb_data directly. Load -> branch pairs are common in CoreMark
(list_find idx/next walks, state-machine byte scans, list-sort compares).
Past lessons say EX-only trims are capped by the IF lfsr -> pc family
(+1.44%), so this hypothesis also needs the cycle saving to clear the bar.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move branch/jump resolution from EX to MEM. Cycle behaviour for every
redirect stays identical, and load -> branch pairs lose their bubble.

1. EX no longer compares. Delete cmp_a/cmp_b and the p1_*/p2_* select
   flops. A branch's operands go through the existing rs1/rs2 networks,
   which are already captured post-forward into EX/MEM.rs1_val/rs2_val.
   Give these their own compare copies, cmp1_q/cmp2_q (D = rs1/rs2, with
   no m_a/m_b mux, so the compare starts at pure flops).
2. EX registers only cond-independent redirect info into EX/MEM, all
   computed from ID/EX flops or the AGU exactly as today:
     - fire_u_q: JALR, or an un-predicted / out-of-window JAL.
     - fire_t_q: predicted not-taken, aligned target.
     - fire_n_q: predicted taken.
     - c_eq/c_lt/c_ltu/c_inv branch selects.
     - redirect target flops tgt_q/pc4_q/alt_q, as today's
       redirect_tgt_q/redirect_pc4_q/redirect_alt_q.
   The fire bits drop fire_ok's !redirect_q/!stall terms. They are
   cleared by the existing kill zeroing, together with ctrl/valid.
3. MEM computes cond, and from it the redirect, combinationally:
     cond     = ((c_eq&eq) | (c_lt&lt) | (c_ltu&ltu)) ^ c_inv
                on opa/opb
     opa      = ld1_q ? MEM/WB.wb_data : cmp1_q    (same for opb)
     redirect = fire_u_q | (cond ? fire_t_q : fire_n_q)
     target   = (alt_q & !cond) ? pc4_q : tgt_q
   The branch sits in EX/MEM for exactly one cycle, because it is not a
   memory op and so no dmem stall can hold it. So redirect fires exactly
   once, in the same cycle today's redirect_q does. The PC mux,
   flush_id and the EX squash (kill -> EX/MEM bubble) consume it
   unchanged.
4. muldiv: m_stall/is_mop no longer take the redirect term. A wrong-path
   M-op in EX during redirect is still bubbled by kill, and flush_id
   still clears ID/EX valid/ctrl. muldiv gets a sync abort (state/done
   -> IDLE on redirect), so a started wrong-path op can never deliver a
   stale result. Only the 4 FSM flops see the late redirect net; the
   operand-latch CE does not.
5. Load -> branch forwarding. In ID, when f1_x/f2_x hits an ID/EX load
   and the fetch word is a branch, register ld1/ld2 (carried through
   ID/EX into EX/MEM), and do not flag load-use. Exempt branches from the
   fetch-word load-use compare with a 4-bit partial opcode decode
   (w[6]&w[5]&!w[4]&!w[2]; the only other match is the reserved 1101011,
   which traps and consumes no operands) folded into the existing
   load_use LUT. The implementer must check that this does not add a LUT
   level to stall_if/stall_id (see step 7). If it does, fall back to
   keeping the bubble and ship steps 1-4 alone.
6. BHT update and RVFI: bht_wdata/branch_taken, the misaligned-taken trap
   and pc_next for branches come from MEM's cond. The BHT write is
   cond -> 1-2 LUTs -> flop D, far off the wall. RVFI rs1/rs2_rdata of an
   ld-forwarded branch come from MEM/WB.wb_data (RVFI-only, pruned).
7. Required measurement (the last four runs skipped it): capture
   `python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options --paths 40` for the
   champion and for the final build, write both option-1 path lists into
   implementation_notes.md, and record the cosim cycle count.
Expected: the EX wall loses the compare -> redirect_q and AGU ->
redirect_tgt_q families, plus 2 of the 7 loads on every bypass-leg bit.
The new MEM compare path (flop -> 1 mux LUT -> carry chain -> 2 LUTs ->
PC mux / 25 ctrl flops) should land around 6.5-7.5 ns, below the 9.1 ns
wall. Fmax gain is capped near +1.4% by the untouched IF family.
Cycles should fall about 2-3% from load -> branch bubbles.

title: 256-entry agree-BHT in distributed LUT-RAM: 4x capacity at a shallower read and ~128 fewer flops
motivation:
r7s2's offline model of the timed CoreMark window (2,922,015 instr,
529,588 cond branches, 13,735 JALR=ret) gives 46,325 conditional
mispredicts for today's 64 x 2-bit pc[7:2] agree-BHT, and 39.6K for a
256-entry agree table (-6.7K redirects x 3 fetch slots ~ -20K cycles,
~-0.45%). All ~60K redirects together are only ~4% of cycles, so no
predictor wins on IPC alone; every predictor/fetch change so far
(r2s2..r10s2) lost 3.5-17% Fmax by adding logic, load or area to the
IF next-PC cone or near the congested EX wall. So a predictor change
here must REMOVE depth and area from IF, not add it.
Today's BHT is 128 plain flops read by a 64:1 mux on pc[7:2]. The r8s0
synthesis report shows GowinSynthesis emits no MUX2_LUT5/6 cells on this
core, so that mux is a ~6-level LUT4 tree (pc[2] alone drives ~64 LUTs),
feeding dir -> pred_b -> next_pc -> pc, the IF family that sits ~0.13 ns
behind the option-1 wall. The write side adds 64 decoded flop enables.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move the agree-BHT into distributed LUT-RAM (the same syn_ramstyle =
"distributed_ram" inference the regfile already uses; lutram=32 today)
and grow it to 256 entries, indexed by pc[9:2]:
  - storage: 16 banks of 16 x 2-bit async-read LUT-RAM (RAM16SDP-class),
    read address pc[5:2] straight from the PC flop, then a 16:1 bank mux
    on pc[9:6]. Depth = 1 RAM read + ~4 LUT4 levels, i.e. one level
    SHALLOWER than today's 64:1 flop mux, and pc[2] fanout drops from
    ~64 LUTs to ~16 RAM address pins.
  - area: -128 FF, -64 write-enable decodes, -~130-LUT read tree; +16
    LUT-RAM cells + ~30 LUT bank mux. Net fewer cells near IF/ID, which
    after r10s1/r10s2 is the direction that helps the congested EX wall.
  - no reset on LUT-RAM: store (ctr ^ 2'b10), so an all-zero RAM reads
    as weakly-agree = today's reset value (pure BTFN cold start). A
    `ifdef VERILATOR reset loop zeroes it (as reg_file does) so cosim
    starts identical; formal/FPGA see arbitrary initial contents, which
    is safe because EX verifies every prediction (IF still never
    predicts a misaligned or out-of-window target).
  - write port unchanged in behaviour: bht_we/bht_wdata from EX/MEM,
    bht_widx widened to ex_mem.pc[9:2]; ID/EX and EX/MEM keep carrying
    the 2-bit pred_ctr read at fetch (read-before-write same as flops).
Nothing else changes: next_pc select, pred_j/pred_b terms (keep
imem_ready in them), redirect_q/redirect_tgt_q, EX fire logic and every
EX network are untouched, so no new term reaches the EX wall or the PC
mux. Expected: ~-0.45% cycles (model) and Fmax neutral-to-positive from
the shallower, lower-fanout IF read and ~250 fewer cells.
Implementation checks (put numbers in implementation_notes.md):
  1. Parameterise the index width; with 6 bits (64 entries) cosim must
     give exactly 4,442,763 cycles (proves the LUT-RAM + xor-encoding is
     behaviour-identical), then set 8 bits and record the new cycles.
  2. Confirm in the Gowin report that the table mapped to LUT-RAM
     (lutram count rises from 32 by ~16) and FF count drops by ~128; if
     it mapped to flops or BSRAM, fix the attribute before scoring
     (BSRAM would add a clock-to-out on the IF path and must be avoided).
  3. If time permits, capture `python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench
     --all-options` option-1 paths before/after for the IF family.

lesson: - 2026-09-30 hyp-20260930-003-r11s2 (regression, -12.99%): Moving the IF agree-BHT from 64 x 2-bit flops (a 64:1 mux on pc[7:2]) into syn_ramstyle = "distributed_ram" LUT-RAM and growing it to 256 entries on pc[9:2] (16 banks of 16 x 2 plus a 16:1 bank mux, storing ctr ^ 2'b10 so the unreset RAM reads weakly-agree, with the reset loop only under `ifdef VERILATOR`) was pitched as one LUT level shallower and ~250 cells smaller in the IF next-PC cone for a ~0.45% cycle saving, yet scored 215.18 vs 247.30, which implies ~95.2-95.6 MHz vs 109.87 (worst path ~10.5 ns vs 9.10 ns, roughly two to three LUT levels longer; the range spans unchanged and model-predicted cycles, and the implementer again left no notes, cycle count, lutram/FF count or path list although the hypothesis required all of them); a loss that size fits Gowin ignoring the attribute and building 512 flops with an 8-level 2:1-LUT read mux (two levels deeper than the old 64:1), and it also fits r10s1's -12.8% from added area disturbing the EX wall's placement, and the run cannot tell which; so a predictor change that removes logic on paper lost as badly as the additive ones (r7s2 -14%), a storage remap must never be bundled with a table-size change, and any further BHT work must first time the 64-entry LUT-RAM remap alone, with its lutram/FF counts and an option-1 (`--all-options`) path list, as r7s2's rule of no predictor slot without a timing report already requires.

title: Merge EX operand networks 6 -> 4: rs1+cmp_a and rs2+cmp_b share one one-hot AND-OR each
motivation:
The r6s1 champion (247.30, 109.87 MHz, 4,442,763 cycles) sits on a flat
option-1 wall: the shifter bypass loop, cmp -> branch_cond -> redirect_q /
branch_taken, AGU -> redirect_tgt_q and SLT -> lg paths are all within
~30 ps. Every one of them begins at the same bypass sources: the four
EX/MEM leg flops (sum/dif/sh/lg) and MEM/WB.wb_data (fw). Each bit of
those sources now drives SIX 32-bit one-hot AND-OR operand networks
(alu_a, alu_b, rs1, rs2, cmp_a, cmp_b) plus the mem_stage merge, so
their nets are long and spread over ~6 x 32 x 3-4 LUTs.
The lessons give two measured data points on the load of these sources:
r8s1 added one private 6-leg network (sh_a) on the same sources and lost
~9% Fmax, although it removed logic depth elsewhere; r10s2 duplicated
read ports/compare networks and lost ~17%. Adding load to the shared
bypass sources is the most expensive thing seen on this core, so
removing load from them is the untested direction. Trims that removed LUT
levels from one family were capped by the other families (r8s0 flat);
cutting the fanout of the shared sources shortens the first route hop
of every EX family at once.

option-1 wall: the shifter bypass loop, cmp -> branch_cond -> redirect_q /

~30 ps. Every one of them begins at the same bypass sources: the four
EX/MEM leg flops (sum/dif/sh/lg) and MEM/WB.wb_data (fw). Each bit of
those sources now drives SIX 32-bit one-hot AND-OR operand networks
(alu_a, alu_b, rs1, rs2, cmp_a, cmp_b) plus the mem_stage merge, so
their nets are long and spread over ~6 x 32 x 3-4 LUTs.
The lessons give two measured data points on the load of these sources:
r8s1 added one private 6-leg network (sh_a) on the same sources and lost
~9% Fmax, although it removed logic depth elsewhere; r10s2 duplicated
read ports/compare networks and lost ~17%. Adding load to the shared
bypass sources is the most expensive thing seen on this core, so
removing load from them is the untested direction. Trims that removed LUT
levels from one family were capped by the other families (r8s0 flat);
cutting the fanout of the shared sources shortens the first route hop
of every EX family at once.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Delete two of the six EX operand networks, with no change to any cycle
behaviour, so each EX/MEM leg bit and fw bit drops from 7 to 5 loads and
~64 x 3-4 LUTs of operand logic disappear from the region around the EX
wall:
  - src1 (= old rs1 and cmp_a merged): one AND-OR of the 4 class-split
    x legs, fw and in.rs1_val, selected by s1_x/s1_w/s1_r. It feeds the
    AGU (rs1 + imm, mem_addr / JALR target), the branch compare a-side,
    and the RVFI rs1_val. The p1_x/p1_w/p1_r select flops and the op_br
    gating are deleted.
  - src2 (= old rs2 and cmp_b merged): same form on s2_x/s2_w/s2_r. It
    feeds the compare b-side and EX/MEM.write_data (store data, RVFI).
    p2_x/p2_w/p2_r are deleted.
alu_a / alu_b stay exactly as they are (they carry the pc / b_const
legs and feed the ALU, shifter and muldiv).
Each merged network now has 2-3 sinks (compare chain + AGU chain, or
compare chain + write_data flop) instead of 1, but the extra sinks are a
carry-chain input and a flop D pin next to it, while the bypass sources
lose two whole 32-bit networks of load. Expected: option-1 Fmax
109.87 -> ~114-116 MHz (+4-5%) at unchanged 4,442,763 cycles.
Why this is not a repeat: r6s1 (trim C) gave the compare private
networks to take it off the ALU networks' select flops (~64-96 loads per
select). This merge keeps that benefit: the compare joins the rs1/rs2
networks, not alu_a/alu_b, so every select flop still drives exactly one
32-bit network (~32 loads), and the compare stays off the ALU/shifter
selects. What goes away is only the duplicate load on the bypass data
sources. No run has isolated the cost of those two extra networks, and
r8s1 shows one extra network on these sources costs ~9%.
Correctness: with the op_br gating gone, src1/src2 carry real values
for non-branches, but branch_taken is gated by is_branch and
redirect_fire = cond ? (fire_u|fire_t) : (fire_u|fire_n) reduces to
fire_u when fire_t = fire_n = 0, so non-branches never depend on the
compare. RVFI rs1/rs2_val are unchanged (same s1/s2 selects).
Implementer protocol (required, because the score alone cannot
attribute the result): run `python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench
--all-options` (with `--paths 30` if supported) on the unmodified
champion and after the change, and record option-1 Fmax, LUT4/FF counts
and the top path start/end points of both in implementation_notes.md.
If option 1 comes out slower after the merge, also try the variant that
merges only rs2 into cmp_b (store data is a flop D pin, so that sink is
the cheapest) and keep the better one; do not add anything else.

lesson: - 2026-09-30 hyp-20260930-001-r12s0 (regression, -3.23%): Only the fallback half of the planned 6 -> 4 EX operand-network merge landed (the diff folds cmp_b into rs2 as one shared src2 that feeds the compare b-side, EX/MEM.write_data and RVFI rs2_val, and deletes p2_x/p2_w/p2_r and their op_br gating; cmp_a and its p1 flops stay; the implementer left no notes and no before/after `--all-options` report, so it is unknown whether the full rs1+cmp_a merge was tried and came out worse), and it scored 239.31 vs 247.30, which implies ~106.3 MHz vs 109.87 (a ~9.40 ns worst path vs 9.10 ns) if cycles stayed at 4,442,763 as designed; so removing one 32-bit network of load from the shared EX/MEM-leg and fw bypass sources gained nothing, and the extra sinks on the merged compare/store-data net (or the placement shift they caused) cost more than any gain, so r8s1's -9% should not be blamed on bypass-source fanout alone, and the branch compare should keep its private, op_br-gated operand networks from r6s1 rather than share them to cut source fanout.

title: Unified EX datapath: one alu_a/alu_b operand pair feeds ALU, AGU and branch compare (3 of 6 timed operand networks deleted)
motivation:
The r6s1 champion (247.30, ~109.9 MHz, 4,442,763 cycles for 2,922,015
instructions) has a flat EX wall: the shifter bypass loop, compare ->
redirect_q, AGU -> redirect_tgt_q and SLT -> lg, all within ~50 ps.
Every trim in rounds 7-11 lost or came out flat. The consistent finding
of r8s1, r10s1 and r10s2 is that added area and load near this wall cost
several percent of Fmax, even when the new logic is not on the path:
- r8s1's private shifter network lost 9%;
- r10s1's registered buffer lost 12.8%, with only EX-wall paths in its
  top 25;
- r10s2's duplicated read ports and compares lost 17%.
No run has tried the opposite, which is taking area and load away from
the wall's shared sources. Today EX builds six 32-bit one-hot operand
networks from the same sources: rs1 (AGU + RVFI), rs2 (store data +
RVFI), alu_a, alu_b, cmp_a and cmp_b. Each of them loads every
EX/MEM leg bit (sum/dif/sh/lg) and every fw bit, and those nets are the
heads of every wall family. For a branch the ALU operands already are
rs1/rs2 (a_rs=1, b_rs=1). For a load or store they already are rs1/imm
(a_rs=1, b_imm=1). So the private cmp networks, the rs1 network and
the separate AGU adder (plus its two compare carry chains and eq tree)
duplicate values that alu_a/alu_b already carry.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make EX a classic single-operand-pair datapath with unchanged cycle
behaviour: same stages, forwarding, load-use bubble, registered
redirect with squash, predictor and muldiv handshake. CoreMark cycles
should stay exactly 4,442,763.
1. AGU = ALU adder. Loads and stores already have alu_a = rs1 and
   alu_b = imm. JALR changes from (a=pc, b=4) to (a=rs1, b=imm): in ID,
   move op_jalr out of a_pc/b_four and into a_rs/b_imm. agu becomes
   alu_sum. It feeds EX/MEM.mem_addr (still a plain flop, so Gowin
   keeps absorbing it into the dmem BSRAM address register), mem_mis,
   misalign_jump and the JALR redirect target. The separate
   rs1 + in.imm adder is deleted.
2. JALR link. pc4 (the existing EX incrementer, off ID/EX.pc) moves onto
   the lg leg. JALR's class becomes k.lg with an ID-registered r_link
   bit, and EX/MEM.lg D becomes
   ({32{r_mres}} & m_result) | ({32{r_link}} & pc4) | alu_lg, where
   r_* are zero for the other classes. Both new terms are early, from
   flops or the flop + incrementer. JAL keeps pc + 4 through the adder
   (a_pc, b_four) on the sum leg. LUI and AUIPC are unchanged.
3. Branch compare on alu_a/alu_b. The alu module exports eq (a == b),
   lt and ltu. lt/ltu are the chains SLT/SLTU already use, so they are
   shared rather than duplicated. branch_cond =
   ((c_eq&eq)|(c_lt&lt)|(c_ltu&ltu)) ^ c_inv feeds the unchanged Ft/Fn
   fire terms and redirect_q. Delete the cmp_a/cmp_b networks and the
   p1_*/p2_* select flops from id_ex_t and id_stage.
4. Keep the rs1 network (s1_* selects) in RTL, but make it feed only
   EX/MEM.rs1_val, which is RVFI-only, so synthesis prunes it from the
   timed netlist. Keep rs2 for store data.
The timed EX then has 3 operand networks (alu_a, alu_b, rs2) instead of
6, so each EX/MEM leg bit and fw bit drops from ~6 network loads to 3.
Also gone: one 32-bit adder, two compare carry chains, a 32-bit eq tree
and ~20 select flops, about 250-300 LUT4 (~8% of 3393) next to the wall.
The heads of every wall family (x/w source -> first AND-OR LUT) get
lighter, and placement has room to pull the loop tighter.
Expected: +4 to +8% Fmax at unchanged cycles.
Main risk: compare -> redirect_q now starts from alu_a/alu_b, which also
drive the shifter, the adders and logic (+1 load per bit for the eq
tree). The cmp networks were made private in r6s1 for that reason.
Required procedure, one step per run so the score can be attributed:
  (a) capture the champion's option-1 path list
      (`python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options --paths 40`);
  (b) implement steps 1+2+4 only (AGU/rs1 network gone, private cmp
      networks kept) and re-time with the same command;
  (c) add step 3 and re-time.
Submit whichever of (b)/(c) has the higher option-1 Fmax. Record
all three path lists, the LUT/FF counts and the cosim cycle count in
implementation_notes.md.

lesson: - 2026-09-30 hyp-20260930-002-r12s1 (regression, -3.25%): Cutting EX from six timed operand networks to three (the ALU adder became the AGU for load/store addresses and the JALR target, JALR's pc+4 link moved onto the lg leg through a new r_link term, the branch compare moved onto alu_a/alu_b using the ALU's SLT/SLTU chains plus a new eq, and cmp_a/cmp_b, their p1/p2 select flops and the separate rs1+imm adder were deleted, with rs1 left feeding only RVFI) scored 239.27, which implies ~106.3 MHz vs 109.87 if cycles stayed at 4,442,763 as designed (not confirmed), within 0.02% of same-round r12s0 (239.31), which merged only cmp_b into rs2; so removing three networks, an adder and two compare chains (~250-300 LUT4 by the hypothesis' estimate, not counted) gained nothing over removing one, and the change both runs share, the compare -> redirect_q path now starting from a shared operand net instead of r6s1's private op_br-gated cmp network, is the likeliest cause of the ~3.2% loss (other suspects here: the new redirect_tgt_q, mem_addr and misalign sinks on alu_sum, which is inside the bypass loop and now also has to reach the dmem BSRAM address register that r3s0 had given its own AGU, and the r_link & pc4 term added to the D-input of EX/MEM.lg, a wall endpoint); the implementer again left no notes, path lists or LUT counts, and the submitted diff is step (c) with no record that step (b) was timed alone, so the AGU merge with the private compare networks kept is still unmeasured; adding area near the EX wall has cost Fmax (r8s1, r10s1, r10s2) but taking it away has not given any back, so stop merging operand networks to cut bypass-source fanout, keep the private compare networks, and try step (b) alone only with a before/after `--all-options` path list.

title: Agree-BHT storage remap alone: 64x2 flops -> 4 banks of 16x2 LUT-RAM, same size and index, cycle-identical
motivation:
Every predictor change since r6s1 has lost Fmax (r7s2 RAS -14%, r11s2
256-entry LUT-RAM BHT -13%), and r11s2's own lesson says the next BHT
step must time the 64-entry LUT-RAM remap ALONE, with no size change
and with lutram/FF counts and an option-1 path list, because the run
could not tell "Gowin ignored the attribute and built a deeper flop
mux" from "the extra area moved the EX wall".
Pure direction/target prediction is capped at ~4% of cycles (60K
redirects x 3 slots), so a predictor slot can only pay through Fmax or
area. Today the agree-BHT is the biggest predictor structure in the
design and it sits in the IF next-PC family, 0.13 ns behind the EX wall:
  - 128 flops, each with its own clock enable. The enable is the 64-way
    decode of EX/MEM.pc[7:2] AND bht_we, and bht_we contains
    !stall_ex_mem = !(dmem_ready && mem_op). That adds a lfsr-sourced
    dmem_ready -> 64 CE-LUTs -> 128 FF load to the same stall net that
    drives the whole EX/MEM clock enable.
  - The read is a 64:1 x 2-bit mux on the PC flop (pc[7:2] fan out to
    all of it), in front of dir -> pred_b -> next_pc -> pc.
The regfile already shows that this exact inference style (async read,
sync write, syn_ramstyle = "distributed_ram") maps to Gowin LUT-RAM on
this flow (r3s0).

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Keep the predictor behaviour bit-for-bit identical: same 64 entries,
same pc[7:2] index, same 2-bit agree counters, same update rule, same
cold value (weakly-agree). Change only how it is stored and enabled.
1. Storage: four banks of 16 x 2 bits, bank = pc[7:6], row = pc[5:2],
   each declared as its own `(* syn_ramstyle = "distributed_ram" *)
   logic [1:0] bank_k [0:15]` with async read and one sync write port.
   Do not use a single 64-deep array, because r11s2's 16:1 bank mux
   over many banks is exactly what is being isolated here. Read =
   4:1 mux of the four bank outputs by pc[7:6] (one LUT level per bit).
2. Cold value without a reset loop: store ctr ^ 2'b10, so an all-zero
   (unwritten, power-up INIT=0) row reads as 2'b10 = weakly agree, as
   the flop reset does today. Keep a reset-clear loop only under
   `ifdef VERILATOR`, the same as reg_file.sv, so cocotb/cosim
   back-to-back runs start cold. Formal sees arbitrary contents, which
   is harmless: the BHT only steers prediction, and EX verifies every
   prediction.
3. Write enable: bht_we = ex_mem.valid && ex_mem.ctrl.is_branch. Drop
   !stall_ex_mem. This is exactly equivalent: a branch in EX/MEM has
   no memory op, so dmem_stall (= !dmem_ready && mem_op) is 0 whenever
   bht_we could be 1, and EX/MEM has no other stall source. This takes
   the lfsr dmem_ready net off the predictor completely. Per-bank
   WE = bht_we && (widx[5:4] == k), and the write row is widx[3:0].
Expected effect: CoreMark cycles unchanged (4,442,763; the implementer
must confirm). Area drops by ~128 FF and roughly 100-150 LUT4 (the
64:1 read mux and the 64 CE decodes), replaced by ~8 RAM16 cells and
a 2-LUT read mux. This takes about two LUT levels and the pc[7:2]
fanout out of the IF next-PC family, and adds no load to any EX-wall
net. This does not beat the flat EX wall by itself; the upside is the
placement relief (r10s1 showed that area near the wall moves it by
several percent), so the honest expectation is small. The run is also
the calibration r11s2 asked for, so its report is required even if it
scores flat.
Required evidence (put it in implementation_notes.md):
  - Synthesis resource report: the lutram / RAM16SDP count must go up
    by the expected ~4-8 cells and the FF count must fall by ~128. If
    FF did not fall, Gowin ignored the attribute: STOP and report it;
    do not ship a flop version.
  - `python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options --paths 40`
    before and after, listing the IF-family (pc / bht / pred_b) paths
    and the first EX-wall path.
  - Cosim cycle count, which must equal the champion's.
Revert rule: if option-1 Fmax falls by more than 1% against the
before-run, keep the flops and record the result. Do not bundle any
other change.

title: Load-use bubble diet: store-data loads forwarded in MEM from MEM/WB.wb_data, and no load-use stall on fake rs1/rs2 fields
motivation:
The ~110 MHz r6s1 champion sits on a flat option-1 timing wall (12+ paths
within ~32 ps over five families). Every Fmax trim since r8s0 scored between
-16% and 0%, because the best any one-family trim can gain is that family's
gap to the next one (~0.15-1.4%). The remaining lever is cycles saved by logic
that sits on none of those families. The load-use interlock is conservative
in two ways, and both are cheap to fix away from the EX bypass loop:
(1) A store whose rs2 (store data) is the rd of the load directly ahead
stalls for one bubble. The store data is not needed until MEM, and by then
the load is in MEM/WB, with its aligned value already registered in
MEM/WB.wb_data. MEM/WB holds its data fields during a dmem stall
(hold_mem_wb), so that value stays put for as long as the store waits.
(2) hazard_unit compares id_ex.rd against fetch_word[19:15] and [24:20] for

hypothesis.motivation:
The ~110 MHz r6s1 champion sits on a flat option-1 timing wall (12+ paths
within ~32 ps over five families). Every Fmax trim since r8s0 scored between
-16% and 0%, because the best any one-family trim can gain is that family's
gap to the next one (~0.15-1.4%). The remaining lever is cycles saved by logic
that sits on none of those families. The load-use interlock is conservative
in two ways, and both are cheap to fix away from the EX bypass loop:
(1) A store whose rs2 (store data) is the rd of the load directly ahead
stalls for one bubble. The store data is not needed until MEM, and by then
the load is in MEM/WB, with its aligned value already registered in
MEM/WB.wb_data. MEM/WB holds its data fields during a dmem stall
(hold_mem_wb), so that value stays put for as long as the store waits.
(2) hazard_unit compares id_ex.rd against fetch_word[19:15] and [24:20] for
every opcode. For I-type (OP-IMM, LOAD, JALR) bits [24:20] are imm[4:0], and
for LUI/AUIPC/JAL bits [19:15] are immediate bits too. Common CoreMark
sequences (`lw a2,..; lw a3,12(a1)`, `lw aX,..; addi aY,aY,12/8/4`) then
take a spurious bubble. The PC also re-fetches the consumer after every

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Two IPC-only changes, both kept off the EX operand AND-ORs, the ALU/compare
chains, redirect_q/redirect_tgt_q and the IF next-PC cone.
A. Store-data forward in MEM. In ID, flag st_ld = (opcode == STORE) &&
   ID/EX.mem_read && ID/EX.rd != 0 && ID/EX.rd == fetch_word[24:20] &&
   ID/EX.rd != fetch_word[19:15]. Register it into ID/EX; it is never set
   when the load also feeds the address, since that is a true AGU load-use.
   hazard_unit takes the rs2 term out of load_use for this case (see B for
   the exact form). ex_stage passes the flag to EX/MEM as st_fwd (cleared by
   kill like ctrl). In mem_stage the store data is
   `st_fwd ? mem_wb.wb_data : in.write_data`, placed before the byte-lane
   replication. That is flop -> 1 LUT -> existing wdata_rep mux -> dmem
   BSRAM din, a short path with no new leg in any EX network. The EX/MEM
   rs2_val used for RVFI rs2_rdata gets the same mux when captured into
   MEM/WB (RVFI-only, pruned in the timed netlist). Correctness under dmem
   stalls:
     - If the load stalls in MEM, the store stays held in EX (ID/EX and
       EX/MEM hold), and st_fwd only takes effect once the store is in
       EX/MEM.
     - If the store stalls in MEM, hold_mem_wb keeps MEM/WB.wb_data (the
       load's value), so the forwarded data stays correct for every
       retry cycle.
     - A misaligned or trapping load has reg_write cleared in EX. ID only
       sees ID/EX (pre-trap) ctrl, so st_fwd must also be gated in MEM by
       mem_wb.ctrl.reg_write (a registered bit). If that bit is clear, the
       store falls back to the EX-captured write_data. This is
       architecturally correct because a trapping load writes no rd, so the
       store's rs2 is the older value that EX forwarded.
   To make that fallback correct, the store's normal EX rs2 select must
   still be computed. For an st_fwd store, EX's s2 x select points at the
   load's sum leg (its address), so write_data would be wrong. Therefore ID
   re-derives the store's s2 select as if the load did not exist: the
   next-older writer via EX/MEM (w) or the regfile (r). forward_unit gains
   an `ignore_x` input that turns sel_x off and lets sel_w/sel_rf resolve,
   driven by the same st_ld term, for the s2 network only. It is an ID-side
   select-flop change: same flops, same EX AND-OR.
B. Precise load-use operand usage. uses_rs1 = !(LUI | AUIPC | JAL) and
   uses_rs2 = OP | BRANCH | (STORE && !st_ld_rs2_only), all from
   fetch_word[6:0]. Final form:
     load_use = mem_read_q && rd_nz_q &&
                ((eq1 && uses_rs1) || (eq2 && uses_rs2)).
   eq1/eq2 already need a 2-level 5-bit compare, so the opcode gate should
   fold into the last LUT (<= 4 inputs: eq1, eq2, u1, u2). Precompute u1/u2
   from the 7 opcode bits in parallel with the compares, never in series.
   ID/EX.mem_read and rd_nz can be one registered bit (lu_q =
   mem_read && rd != 0).
Expected effect: fewer load-use bubbles and fewer consumer re-fetches.
Fmax stays within noise, because the only new logic on a timed path is
one LUT on the MEM write data (not in any co-critical family) and the
ID-side forward select for s2. The opcode gate in the load_use ->
stall_if/stall_id cone is the main risk (r11s1 listed it as a suspect), so
the implementer must check it.
REQUIRED MEASUREMENTS (write them to implementation_notes.md):
  1. Before any change, run the Python ISS / cosim trace for CoreMark and
     count (a) load -> store-data-only adjacent pairs, (b) spurious
     load-use matches (field matches but the opcode does not use it), and
     (c) total load-use bubbles. If a + b < 1.5% of the 4,442,763 cycles,
     write that in the notes and still implement, but expect a
     no-acceptance result.
  2. Report the cycles after the change (expect 4,442,763 minus about
     1.28 x (a + b)).
  3. Run `python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options --paths 40`
     before and after. If option-1 Fmax drops by more than 1% and the new
     worst path runs through the load_use opcode gate, drop change B and
     keep only A (A has no logic in the stall cone apart from removing the
     rs2 term for st_ld, which is a registered-bit AND).

lesson: - 2026-09-30 hyp-20260930-001-r13s0 (regression, -3.98%): The load-use "bubble diet" (store data late-forwarded in MEM from MEM/WB.wb_data on a registered m2/st_fwd bit, plus opcode-only uses_rs1/uses_rs2 gates so immediate bits in the rs1/rs2 fields stop matching) was meant to be IPC-only but scored 237.46 vs 247.30, which implies ~105.5 MHz vs 109.87 at unchanged cycles, or ~102-104 MHz if the hoped-for 1.5-3% of cycles were saved (the implementer left no pair counts, cycle count or path list, and kept B, so the required "drop B if the worst path runs through the opcode gate" check is unrecorded); the hypothesis' claim that A alone adds only a registered-bit AND to the stall cone was wrong, because the store is still the raw imem word in ID when load_use has to decide, so both A and B put a fetch-word opcode decode into load_use -> stall_if/stall_id (the PC CE, shared with the lfsr -> pc family ~0.13 ns behind the wall), and A also added an opcode + rs1-inequality ignore_x term to the s2 forward-select D-inputs; with r11s1 (-4.82%) this is the second ~4-5% loss in a run that added a fetch-word opcode term to the load_use cone, so while ID decodes straight from io_imemData, treat that cone and the forward-select D-inputs as having no slack and do not relax load-use again, since the bubbles it can remove (a few % of cycles at most) cannot pay for the Fmax it costs.

title: 4-stage retire: write the regfile from MEM, delete the MEM/WB forwarding leg from all six EX operand networks
motivation:
On the r6s1 champion (~109.9 MHz, 4,442,763 cycles) every EX operand
network (s1, s2, a, b, p1, p2) is a one-hot AND-OR of the four
class-split EX/MEM legs, MEM/WB.wb_data (fw), the ID-registered regfile
value and (a/b) pc/b_const: 6-7 terms, i.e. 2 LUT4 levels plus the
routing of fw, a 32-bit net fanning out to 6 networks (~192 loads)
plus the MEM/WB hold CE. The fw leg exists only because the regfile is
written one stage late (from MEM/WB). The bypass-loop family, the
compare -> redirect_q family and the AGU -> redirect_tgt_q family all
start at these operand networks. r9s1 showed that removing fw from EX
does not create a slower path elsewhere (its ID pre-merge flop fed
from mem_stage's wb_data D-input stayed within ~0.8% of the wall), and
that the EX side alone could reach at least the IF cap; this change
removes fw with zero interlock bubbles (r9s1 lost only because it paid
~2.2% extra cycles for its x_stall).

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure retirement into 4 timed stages (IF, ID, EX, MEM+WB):
the regfile write port is driven directly by the MEM stage
(w_en = EX/MEM.valid && ctrl.reg_write && !dmem_stall, w_addr =
EX/MEM.rd, w_data = mem_stage's combinational wb_data), so a producer
two instructions ahead is already in the regfile (write-first bypass)
when its consumer is read in ID. Then:
  * forward_unit's sel_w case disappears: the distance-2 producer is
    in EX/MEM while the consumer is in ID, so the write-first regfile
    read already returns its value; the one-hot selects become x (4
    class legs) and r only. Delete s1_w/s2_w/a_w/b_w/p1_w/p2_w and
    the fw input of ex_stage, so every EX operand network loses one
    32-bit leg (a/b: 7 -> 6 terms, others 6 -> 5).
  * dmem stall: stall_id already holds ID/EX while a load waits, so
    the consumer re-reads the regfile each cycle and captures the
    write-first load data on the edge the load completes (w_en is
    gated by !dmem_stall so a stalled load never writes garbage).
    Load-use distance 1 keeps its single bubble: the consumer sits in
    ID while the load is in MEM and reads the loaded value through
    the write-first bypass, exactly the cycle it previously took fw.
  * the MEM/WB register only feeds RVFI (pruned from the timed
    netlist); keep it for RVFI with rd_wdata = its registered wb_data,
    and keep rvfi_order/valid on it (retirement one cycle after the
    regfile write is fine: nothing architectural reads MEM/WB). The
    hold_mem_wb data-retention rule is no longer needed for
    forwarding (keep valid clear on hold so no double retire).
IPC is unchanged by construction (same bubbles, same redirect,
same muldiv), so fitness moves only with Fmax. The removed fw fanout
and the one fewer leg in all six networks shorten the bypass loop,
the compare -> redirect_q path and the AGU -> redirect_tgt_q path by
up to one LUT level each. The new path (dmem BSRAM -> load align ->
wb_data -> write-first mux -> ID/EX rs_val flop) is the one r9s1
already timed within ~0.8% of the wall; keep it to align + class
merge + ONE write-first LUT by precomputing the w_addr==rs compare
from the EX/MEM.rd flop and the fetch word (both early) and by
putting mem_to_reg/class selects (flops) ahead of the late load data.
Risk: the IF next-PC family (fetch word -> pre-decode -> pc+imm ->
pc) was measured ~0.13 ns behind the wall and is not touched, which
caps the gain unless the operand-network shortening also relieves
placement around the IF cone; the implementer MUST capture
`python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options --paths 40` before
and after and record both lists plus LUT/FF counts in

title: Agree-BHT as 4 banks of 16x2 LUT-RAM (size-neutral remap, measured) - the unrun r12s2 calibration
motivation:
The r7s2 ISS model (2,922,015 instr, 4,442,763 cycles; 529,588 branches,
46,325 mispredicts on the 64 x 2-bit agree-BHT, 13,735 rets) caps every
pure direction/target predictor at ~4.0% of cycles (all ~60K redirects),
below the 4.6% bar, so a predictor slot can only pay through Fmax or
area. The one predictor structure that sits in the timed netlist and has
never been measured is the BHT storage itself: 128 flops read by a 64:1
mux on pc[7:2] (3+ LUT levels, ~40 LUT4 plus 128 FF with 64 decoded
write enables) placed right next to the IF next-PC family that is only
0.13 ns behind the EX wall. r11s2 bundled a LUT-RAM remap with a 4x
table growth and lost 13%; r12s2 (remap alone) was a no-op run (empty
diff, bit-identical 247.30), so the calibration LESSONS asks for before
any further BHT work is still missing. Area removed near the congested
EX wall is the one kind of change that has not yet been measured on
this flow when landed alone and verified.

title: Three-leg EX/MEM (one ADDSUB chain, dif leg deleted) + one sign-flipped branch compare chain
motivation:
r8s0's option-1 report on the r6s1 champion (109.868 MHz, 4,442,763 cycles)
names the flat EX wall: (1) ID/EX.pc -> alu_a -> shifter -> EX/MEM.sh, where
alu_a is THREE LUT levels because it is a 7-leg AND-OR (4 class-split EX/MEM
x legs + fw + rs1_val + pc); (4) p1_x.sub -> cmp_a -> eq/lt/ltu -> 7-input
cond (2 LUTs) -> Ft/Fn pick -> redirect_q. r8s0 fixed (1) by adding ID-side
a_val flops and came out flat because (4) was left 14 ps behind; r9s0/r10s0
fixed (4) with per-leg fire-on bits + sync clear and lost. No run has yet
reduced the NUMBER OF BYPASS LEGS, which shortens every operand network and
removes a 32-bit load from alu_a/alu_b and every EX/MEM source at once, and
no run has shrunk the compare -> cond logic without touching the redirect_q
flop form. The dif (SUB-only) leg is the only EX/MEM leg with a single
producer class, and SUB is rare in CoreMark; SLT/SLTU/BLT/BGE compares use
two separate 32-bit chains each.

a_val flops and came out flat because (4) was left 14 ps behind; r9s0/r10s0
fixed (4) with per-leg fire-on bits + sync clear and lost. No run has yet
reduced the NUMBER OF BYPASS LEGS, which shortens every operand network and
removes a 32-bit load from alu_a/alu_b and every EX/MEM source at once, and
no run has shrunk the compare -> cond logic without touching the redirect_q

producer class, and SUB is rare in CoreMark; SLT/SLTU/BLT/BGE compares use

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Two IPC-neutral changes, each deleting logic from the wall, adding none to
the IF next-PC cone, to redirect_q's flop form, or to any ID/EX D-input that
depends on a late net (only on ID-decoded opcode bits of the fetch word,
like the existing r_* / c_* flops).
A. One add/sub chain. alu.sv computes as = a + (b ^ {32{r_sub}}) + r_sub as
   ONE expression (Gowin ALU ADDSUB mode; r_sub is an ID-registered flop that
   is valid a full cycle early). The `sum` leg carries ADD/ADDI/LUI/AUIPC/
   link AND SUB. The `dif` leg, EX/MEM.dif (32 FFs) and xsel_t.sub are
   deleted: xsel_t becomes {add, sh, lg} (k.add = r_add|r_sub for non-M
   ops). Every class-split x select (s1/s2/a/b/p1/p2) loses one leg, so
   alu_a drops from 7 legs (3 LUT levels) to 6 legs (2 levels) with no
   ID-side a_val flops, and rs1/rs2/cmp_a/cmp_b/alu_b drop from 6 to 5.
   mem_stage's write-back merge becomes 3-way. SLT/SLTU in lg keep their
   current separate lt/ltu expressions (do not move them onto the adder
   chain: r6s0's bundle did that and cannot be credited).
B. Branch compare on one magnitude chain. In ID, register c_sgn = (f3[2:1]
   == 2'b10) (BLT/BGE) next to c_eq/c_inv (c_lt/c_ltu are deleted). EX
   computes ltx = {cmp_a[31]^c_sgn, cmp_a[30:0]} < {cmp_b[31]^c_sgn,
   cmp_b[30:0]} (signed compare == unsigned compare with flipped MSBs; the
   MSB enters the chain last, so its XOR is off the critical carry) and keeps
   cmp_eq. branch_cond = (c_eq ? cmp_eq : ltx) ^ c_inv: 4 inputs, ONE LUT
   instead of two, and one fewer 32-bit chain loading cmp_a/cmp_b. The Ft/Fn
   pick, fire terms, redirect_q/redirect_tgt_q flops, squash and target mux
   stay byte-identical. misalign_branch / reg_write clear keep using
   branch_taken as today.
Expected: family 1 loses a LUT level + route hop (~0.5-0.7 ns), family 4
loses one LUT level (~0.5 ns), and every bypass source loses 1-2 loads per
bit. The untouched IF lfsr -> pc family (~0.13 ns behind) caps a pure EX
gain near +1.4% unless the lighter EX placement also relieves it (r10s1
showed EX-area changes move IF-adjacent placement by several percent), so
the realistic range is +1..+5%. Cycles stay at 4,442,763 by construction.
Implementer MUST: run `python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options
--paths 40` on the unchanged core and after A alone and after A+B, record
option-1 Fmax, top-40 paths, LUT4/FF counts and the cosim cycle count in
implementation_notes.md; if A+B is below A alone on option 1, submit A
alone; if A alone is >1% below 109.87 MHz on option 1, report its new
limiter and submit nothing else stacked on it.

lesson: - 2026-09-30 hyp-20260930-001-r14s0 (regression, -6.35%): Folding SUB into the ADD chain (`sum = a + (b ^ {32{r_sub}}) + r_sub` on an ID-registered r_sub, with the dif leg, EX/MEM.dif and xsel_t.sub deleted so every class-split operand AND-OR loses a leg; the diff shows only part A, since c_lt/c_ltu remain in id_ex_t and the single sign-flipped compare chain never landed) scored 231.59 vs 247.30, which implies ~102.9 MHz vs 109.87 (a ~9.72 ns worst path vs 9.10 ns) at the by-construction 4,442,763 cycles, with no notes or `--all-options` path list; the likely cause is that the b-inversion and carry-in now sit in front of the carry chain on the sum leg, which nearly every CoreMark producer (ADD/ADDI/LUI/AUIPC/link) uses and every bypass consumer reads, to save a SUB-only leg that is rarely selected; this is the third run (after r12s0 and r12s1) where cutting bypass legs or networks lost Fmax, so keep the separate pure `a + b` sum and `a - b` dif chains, and don't remove a rarely used leg by adding logic to a hot one.

title: Relocate load-use interlock from the ID fetch-word compare to a registered EX hold
motivation:
In the r6s1 champion (109.87 MHz option 1, 4,442,763 cycles), ID finds the
load-use hazard by comparing the raw fetch word (io_imemData[19:15] /
[24:20]; in the timed netlist that is the lfsr) with ID/EX.rd. The compare
feeds three places: stall_if (the PC CE), stall_id (the CE of about 300
ID/EX data and select flops) and flush_id (the ID/EX valid/ctrl clear).
Two runs added a single fetch-word opcode term to this cone: r11s1 lost
4.8% and r13s0 lost 4.0%. So the path lfsr -> 5-bit compare -> stall ->
high-fanout CE is the most timing-sensitive control cone on the core. It
sits in the IF lfsr -> pc family, which runs 0.13 ns behind the wall, and
r9s1 showed that this family caps any gain on the EX side at about +1.4%.
So far every run has added terms to this cone (r11s1, r13s0) or tried to
hide it behind a fetch buffer (r10s2). None has taken the compare out of it.

hypothesis.motivation:
In the r6s1 champion (109.87 MHz option 1, 4,442,763 cycles), ID finds the
load-use hazard by comparing the raw fetch word (io_imemData[19:15] /
[24:20]; in the timed netlist that is the lfsr) with ID/EX.rd. The compare
feeds three places: stall_if (the PC CE), stall_id (the CE of about 300
ID/EX data and select flops) and flush_id (the ID/EX valid/ctrl clear).

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move load-use detection one stage later, as a registered hold in EX shaped
like the existing m_stall. By design IPC is unchanged: each load-use pair
still costs one bubble, but the bubble goes in between EX and EX/MEM rather
than between ID and EX. One refetch slot is still lost, one cycle later,
so the cycle count is the same statistically but not bit-identical under
the random imem stalls.

1. ID. Delete load_use_hazard. A consumer at distance 1 from a load enters
   ID/EX normally. ID already computes f1_x/f2_x against ID/EX.rd. Add one
   ID/EX data bit, lu <= ctrl_q.mem_read && (f1_x || f2_x). This is exactly
   today's load_use condition, including its spurious matches on non-rs
   fields, so the number of bubbles stays the same.
2. EX. Define lu_hold = in.valid && in.lu && !redirect_q, built only from
   flops. It acts like m_stall:
   - it joins `kill`, so EX/MEM captures a bubble;
   - stall_if and stall_id take this early flop signal instead of the
     fetch-word compare, so the PC and ID/EX hold;
   - it gates the muldiv start (is_mop) and fire_ok.
3. Select conversion, using only the flops' dedicated sync set/reset pins
   and no D-side LUT. On the hold edge (lu_hold && !dmem_stall) the load
   moves from EX/MEM to MEM/WB, so every class-split x select of the held
   entry (s1/s2/a/b/p1/p2) becomes its w select: the x flops sync-reset,
   each w flop sync-sets when its x vector was non-zero, and lu is cleared.
   No lu_done flop is needed. While the load is dmem-stalled in MEM the
   whole pipeline stays frozen, as today.
4. Misaligned-load corner. Today a distance-1 consumer of a trapping
   (misaligned) load sees reg_write already cleared, because load_use
   delays it by one cycle. After this change it would convert to a stale w
   leg instead. Fix it with the mechanism already used for trapping
   JAL/JALR: a load with mem_mis redirects to pc+4, which kills the
   consumer and makes it re-decode. Concretely:
   - fire_u gains `in.ctrl.mem_read && mem_mis`, where mem_mis comes from
     agu[1:0], the first two carry bits and so early;
   - tgt_seq gains `|| in.ctrl.mem_read`, so the target is pc4.
   This never fires in CoreMark. The late input of the fire select stays
   branch_cond.
5. hazard_unit loses its if_id_rs1/rs2, id_ex_rd and id_ex_mem_read inputs
   and gains lu_hold:
   - stall_if = stall_id = imem_stall | dmem_stall | m_stall | lu_hold;
   - flush_id = redirect && !dmem_stall.

Result: no logic that depends on the fetch word reaches the PC CE, the
ID/EX CE or flush_id. The ~300-load stall_id CE net is driven only from
flops (lfsr ready bits, m_stall, lu_hold). The IF family keeps only its
pre-decode D-side paths.

Expected effect. The IF/ID CE cone loses about 3 LUT levels and a late
high-fanout net. That relieves the family that capped r9s1, and it frees
placement around ID/EX, which r10s1 showed can move the EX wall by several
percent. The EX wall itself only gains early flop terms (kill, fire_ok,
is_mop, fire_u). The upside is uncertain: it depends on how much of the
flat wall is caused by congestion from the late CE net.

Required measurement: record an option-1 path list (`python3 -m
tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options --paths 40`) before and after the
change, plus the CoreMark cycle count. If Fmax does not move, report which
path is worst, so this result can be attributed.

title: Agree-gshare: XOR retired global history into the 64-entry flop BHT select, folded into the 2:1 mux LUTs
motivation:
r7s2's ISS trace: 529,588 conditional branches, 13,735 JALR (all ret),
and 46,325 mispredicts (8.7%) from the current 64 x 2 pc[7:2] agree-BHT.
Each costs ~3 fetch slots, so direction mispredicts are ~139K of 4.44M
cycles (~3.1%). They are the largest predictor-side cost left.
Lessons r11s2 / r13s2 / r7s2 / r10s1 rule out the obvious fixes: no
LUT-RAM or larger BHT, no new next_pc legs, and no fetch buffering.
The only lever still open is WHICH counter the existing 64-entry flop
table returns: its index. Storage, table size, the 64:1 read mux
depth and every next_pc leg stay the same.
This slot has a low ceiling (about +0.5 to +1.5% cycles). It is the
single predictor angle that does not add a leg, a level or storage
to the IF next-PC cone.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Index the BHT by pc[7:2] ^ ghr_q[5:0] (gshare on top of the agree/BTFN
bias) instead of pc[7:2].
- ghr_q is a 6-bit NON-speculative global history of resolved branch
  outcomes. It shifts in ex_mem.branch_taken on the same enable as
  bht_we. There is no wrong-path repair and no new term on the PC,
  redirect or stall logic.
- Timing: pc and ghr_q are both flops. On LUT4, the 64:1 read mux is a
  tree of 2:1 muxes (no MUX2_LUT5/6 cells in the reports), and each
  2:1 LUT has one free input. So sel_i = pc[i] ^ ghr_q[i-2] can fold
  into that level's LUT with no extra depth. Write it as a plain
  `bht[pc[7:2] ^ ghr_q]` and check the mapped depth. If Gowin builds a
  separate XOR level, that is still flop -> 1 LUT -> mux select, which
  is not the late imem_data leg of pred_b.
- Update: carry the 6-bit fetch-time index (bidx) through if_id_t ->
  id_ex_t -> ex_mem_t, next to pred_ctr. bht_widx = ex_mem.bidx, so the
  counter that is trained is the one that was read.
- Also drop the logically redundant !stall_ex_mem term from bht_we.
  A branch in EX/MEM is never a memory op, so dmem_stall is 0 whenever
  bht_we can be 1. This removes ~64 loads from the late dmem_ready
  net. The ghr_q shift uses the same enable.
STEP 0 (offline, before RTL): add an offline model to the ISS branch
trace and count mispredicts for history lengths h = 0..6, using
index = pc[7:2] ^ (ghr & ((1<<h)-1)). Model the update lag as ~3
younger branches fetched before an older one retires. It may be
simpler to fold the history into only the top bits, i.e.
pc[7:2] ^ {ghr[h-1:0], 0...}. Pick the h with the fewest mispredicts.
If no h cuts mispredicts by at least 15% vs 46,325, ship h = 0: only
the bht_we cleanup, and say so in the notes.
Expected: gshare with 4-6 history bits usually cuts mispredicts
~20-35% on CoreMark-like data-dependent branches (core_state
switch, list compares, crcu8 bit test). That is ~10-15K mispredicts,
or ~30-45K cycles (0.7-1.0%). Fmax should be neutral (same storage,
same mux depth, fewer dmem_ready loads).
REQUIRED in implementation_notes: STEP 0 mispredict table, the final
cycle count, and a `python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options
--paths 40` option-1 path list before and after the change. If option-1
Fmax drops by more than 1% and any listed path runs through the BHT
index or the ghr_q flops, revert the index change and keep only the

title: Branch compare on two unsigned carry chains only (eq = !(a<b) & !(b<a), signed lt from sign bits): 2 LUTs after the chain into redirect_q
motivation:
The r8s0 option-1 report on the r6s1 champion (109.868 MHz) names the
branch-compare family twice among five co-critical families:
  #2 p1_x.sub -> cmp_a (2 LUT) -> 6-LUT compare/cond tree ->
     ctrl_with_trap.reg_write (14.395 ns, 1 ps off the worst path)
  #4 p1_x.sub -> cmp_a -> same tree -> Ft/Fn pick -> redirect_q (14.382 ns)
r8s0 trimmed the other families and came out flat (247.28) because it left
this path alone. r9s0 and r10s0 tried to fix it with per-leg fire-on bits and
a rewritten synchronous clear on redirect_q, and lost 1.0-1.6%. Per r10s0,
that rewrite (late stall/redirect_q reaching the flop's clear) is the likely
cause. Nobody has changed the compare itself. After cmp_a/cmp_b there are
six LUT levels. Most of that depth is the 32-bit equality reduce. As a LUT
tree it takes about three LUT4 levels (pairwise XNOR, then AND4, then AND4),
and then cond (eq/lt/ltu x c_eq/c_lt/c_ltu, ^c_inv, two levels) and the
Ft/Fn pick (one level) come after it. lt and ltu already come from carry
chains (`a < b` maps to Gowin ALU chains in this flow), so the equality
tree is the only part of the compare built from LUT levels.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Build every branch outcome from two UNSIGNED carry chains on the existing
private cmp_a/cmp_b networks, and pick the fire bit with 2 LUTs after them:
  ltu_ab = cmp_a < cmp_b   (unsigned, carry chain; exists today as cmp_ltu)
  ltu_ba = cmp_b < cmp_a   (unsigned, carry chain; replaces the XOR/AND eq
                            tree AND the signed cmp_lt chain)
  eq     = !ltu_ab && !ltu_ba
  lt     = (cmp_a[31] ^ cmp_b[31]) ? cmp_a[31] : ltu_ab
Only ltu_ab and ltu_ba arrive late. cmp_a[31]/cmp_b[31] come out of the
2-LUT operand network, well before the chains finish. The branch type
bits (c_eq/c_lt/c_ltu/c_inv) are ID-registered flops. Put all early terms
into an early "late_true" definition plus two early fire candidates:
  sgn_ovr  = c_lt & (cmp_a[31] ^ cmp_b[31])       // early
  late_true = c_eq ? (ltu_ab | ltu_ba)              // "not equal"
                   : ltu_ab                         // lt/ltu
    -> written as  ltu_ab | (c_eq & ltu_ba)         // 1 LUT3, 2 late ins
  cond(late_true) is then:
    c_eq :  !late_true ^ c_inv
    c_lt with sgn_ovr : cmp_a[31] ^ c_inv           (ignores late_true)
    else :  late_true ^ c_inv
  so cond = late_true ? C1 : C0 with early C1/C0:
    C1 = c_eq ? c_inv   : sgn_ovr ? (cmp_a[31] ^ c_inv) : !c_inv
    C0 = c_eq ? !c_inv  : sgn_ovr ? (cmp_a[31] ^ c_inv) :  c_inv
  redirect_fire = late_true ? (C1 ? fire_tt : fire_nn)
                            : (C0 ? fire_tt : fire_nn)
    -> P1/P0 = early, redirect_fire = late_true ? P1 : P0   (1 LUT3)
The redirect_q D path becomes cmp_a (2 LUT) -> carry chain -> LUT3
(late_true) -> LUT3 (pick) -> redirect_q, instead of cmp_a -> 6 LUTs.
branch_taken (EX/MEM.branch_taken, timed through the BHT update and the
redirect_alt_q target pick) uses the same shape: is_branch & (late_true ?
C1 : C0). redirect_q, redirect_tgt_q and the sync reset stay as they are:
no fire-on bits, no clear rewrite, nothing past the edge (r9s2/r10s0).
Also, per r8s0, take misalign_branch out of the reg_write clear. A branch
never has reg_write set, so only misalign_jump || mem_mis clears reg_write.
is_illegal is RVFI-only and gets pruned, so it can keep misalign_branch.
That removes the compare from the D-input of EX/MEM.ctrl.reg_write, which
is family #2 (14.395 ns). Nothing else changes: the ALU keeps its own
lt/ltu chains for SLT/SLTU (lg leg), and the six operand networks, their
select flops and the pipeline timing stay the same. Cycles stay at
4,442,763 by construction because every redirect, branch_taken and trap
bit gets the same value in every cycle.

Why it could pay and what caps it: this takes two of the five co-critical
families (#2, #4) off the wall with no new sinks on the shared bypass
sources (cmp_a/cmp_b stay private and op_br-gated, as r12s0/r12s1 advise
keeping them). The load on cmp_a/cmp_b bits stays about the same: two
chain inputs per bit instead of three (the signed lt chain is gone) plus
zero eq-tree LUTs. The remaining families (pc -> alu_a -> shifter,
muldiv b_q -> res_q, AGU -> redirect_tgt_q, and the IF lfsr -> pc family
about 0.13 ns behind) are not touched, so on paper the gain is capped
near +1.4%. It is proposed as the first measured step of trimming the
whole wall, and as a direct test of whether the compare tree, not the
redirect_q clear logic, is what held r8s0 flat.

lesson: - 2026-09-30 hyp-20260930-001-r15s0 (regression, -3.14%): Rebuilding the branch compare from two unsigned carry chains (cmp_a < cmp_b and cmp_b < cmp_a, eq = neither, signed lt picked by the operand sign bits) and folding the branch type and the Ft/Fn fire candidates into precomputed C1/C0 and P1/P0 terms, so that only a late_true LUT3 and a pick LUT3 follow the chains (plus r8s0's flat reg_write-clear trim), scored 239.54 vs 247.30, which implies ~106.4 MHz vs 109.87 at the by-construction 4,442,763 cycles (the new br_cmp.sv is missing from the captured diff, and there are no notes or path list); the plan treated fire_tt/fire_nn as early, but in ex_stage they are not: fire_ok = in.valid && !redirect_q && !stall carries the dmem stall, and fire_u/fire_t carry pt_ok = pred_taken && !win_out, taken from the top bits of the pc+imm carry chain, so routing them through P1/P0 before the final pick most likely added a LUT level on the stall -> redirect_q and target-adder -> redirect_q paths, which the old `branch_cond ? fire_tt : fire_nn` held to one LUT; with r4s0 (flat), r9s0 (-1.05%) and r10s0 (-1.58%), this is the fourth rework between cmp_a/cmp_b and redirect_q that did no better than leaving it alone, so any later change there must keep stall and the fire terms as direct inputs of redirect_q's last LUT, and the two-chain compare on its own (still unmeasured) should be tried only with a before/after `--all-options` path list.

title: Zero-stall pipelined MUL as a load-like MEM-stage producer (DSP in-reg at EX/MEM edge, mul-use interlock)
motivation:
The r6s1 champion (109.87 MHz, 4,442,763 cycles) has a flat EX wall. Since then
every IPC-neutral trim has come out flat or lost 1-7%, and every fetch or predictor
change has lost 4-17%. The cycle levers that are left must stay away from three
places: the fetch word -> load-use -> PC CE cone, the redirect_q path, and the EX
operand networks. One measured cycle lever is still unclaimed: M-unit stalls.
r11s0 took one of the two MUL stall cycles away and cut cycles from 4,442,763 to
4,347,376 (-2.15%), which implies ~95K MULs per run (matrix_mul_*, and the
crc/state loops through the compiler's index math). It lost only because it read
the DSP product combinationally from fabric a_q/b_q into EX/MEM.lg, a wall
endpoint. Today every MUL/MULH* holds the whole front end for 2 cycles
(m_stall -> stall_if/stall_id), even when no instruction behind it needs the
result. A load, by contrast, costs nothing unless its distance-1 consumer
interlocks.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Handle MUL/MULH/MULHU/MULHSU as a two-stage producer, like a LOAD, with no EX
stall. DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU keep the existing muldiv FSM and m_stall unchanged.
1. Decode: ID registers a new 1-bit class `is_mul` (OP, funct7=1, funct3[2]=0).
   Only the true divide ops keep ctrl.is_muldiv. MUL ops leave EX in one cycle
   like ALU ops (no is_mop, no m_stall).
2. Interlock: hazard_unit's `id_ex_mem_read` input becomes one ID-registered flop,
   `lu_src = mem_read | is_mul`, computed from the decoded fetch word in ID. The
   load-use compare itself is unchanged, so the fetch word -> stall_if cone gets
   no new term (r11s1/r13s0 lesson). A distance-1 consumer of a MUL takes exactly
   the bubble a load-use pair takes. Distance >= 2 consumers forward from MEM/WB
   wb_data as they do for loads.
3. Datapath: the multiplier's operand registers become DSP input registers,
   clocked on the EX -> EX/MEM edge from alu_a/alu_b. Only the 2 sign-extension
   bits need one LUT (a[31] & ID-registered sx bit). These replace the MUL use of
   muldiv's fabric a_q/b_q. The divider keeps its own a_q/b_q latch on `take`.
   The loads on alu_a/alu_b stay the same, because a_q/b_q stop latching for MUL.
   In MEM, the 33x33 product (DSP with registered inputs, and the pipeline
   register if the Gowin template allows it at no latency cost) goes through a
   hi/lo select into mem_stage's write-back merge as a 5th class term
   (c.mul & prod_sel), in parallel with the load-align leg. That merge feeds only
   the MEM/WB.wb_data flop, which is not an EX-wall endpoint. EX/MEM.lg loses its
   `is_muldiv ? m_result : alu_lg` mux for MUL (DIV keeps it). This takes a 2:1
   select off a wall endpoint.
4. Squash: a MUL that redirect_q squashes in EX becomes a bubble as today (valid=0,
   ctrl=0, so c.mul=0). The DSP input regs may capture garbage; nothing reads it.
   A MUL held in EX/MEM by a dmem stall cannot happen (it has no memory op). A MUL
   in EX while EX/MEM is dmem-stalled must hold the DSP input registers: gate
   their CE with !stall_ex_mem (the same CE the EX/MEM register already uses, so
   no new late net).
Cycle model: r11s0 measured one stall per MUL = 2.15%, so both stalls are ~4.3%.
In matrix_mul_*, the `mul; add` pairs at distance 1 give back roughly a third to
half of that as mul-use bubbles. Net -2.5 to -3.5% cycles.
Fmax model: EX loses the lg-leg MUL mux and gains no operand leg. The ID gains one
OR into an existing registered bit. The new path is the DSP input reg -> multiply
-> hi/lo -> wb merge -> MEM/WB.wb_data. With a registered DSP input and no
fabric-to-DSP route in front, it must fit 9.1 ns. If the implementer's option-1
report shows it is over, the fallback is to use the DSP's internal pipeline
register and add a second interlock bubble for distance-2 consumers only when
that path is the limiter. The fallback MUST NOT add a compare to the load-use
cone: drop the change instead.
Implementer MUST: record the cosim cycle count against 4,442,763, record the MUL
count and the mul-use pair count, and run
`python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options --paths 30` after the change.
Put the option-1 path list in implementation_notes. Keep ALTOPS consistent:
under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS, the MEM-stage MUL leg uses the (a+b)^K / (a-b)^K
substitutes computed from the same registered operands.

lesson: - 2026-09-30 hyp-20260930-002-r15s1 (regression, -0.58%): Making MUL/MULH* a zero-stall, load-like producer (is_mul split from a DIV-only is_muldiv; ID/EX.lu_src = mem_read | is_mul feeds the unchanged load-use compare; a new mul_pipe clocks alu_a/alu_b into DSP input registers on the EX -> EX/MEM edge, and its hi/lo product joins mem_stage's write-back merge as a 5th class term in front of MEM/WB.wb_data) scored 245.87 vs 247.30; the implementer left no notes, cycle count, MUL/mul-use counts or path list although the hypothesis required them, but removing both m_stall cycles per MUL at the cost of at most one mul-use bubble must cut cycles by 2.15-4.3% (r11s0 measured ~95K cycles per stall cycle), so Fmax fell to ~104.5-106.9 MHz (a ~9.36-9.57 ns worst path vs 9.10 ns), the same band as r11s0's measured 104.77 MHz; registering the DSP inputs therefore recovered nothing, which refutes this run's premise that r11s0 lost to the fabric a_q/b_q -> DSP route (the champion's a_q/b_q -> multiply -> prod_q path already fits one cycle), and what the two losers share is an unregistered DSP product passing through fabric LUTs (hi/lo select plus the lg mux or the wb merge) into a flop in the same cycle; this run also put 64 DSP-pin loads on the alu_a/alu_b wall nets, since muldiv's a_q/b_q still latch them for the divider (so the "loads stay the same" claim was wrong), and r11s0's one recorded worst path was MEM/WB.wb_data -> redirect_q rather than the multiply, so the loss may show up as a disturbed EX wall rather than on the new leg; the MUL-stall lever is capped at ~4.3% of cycles and two designs have each lost 3-5% Fmax, so read MUL results only from a DSP output register (prod_q), hang no new loads on alu_a/alu_b, and stop spending slots on MUL latency unless a design meets both rules.

title: Exact ID-stage JALR/ret resolution through the existing pure-flop redirect_q (1 bubble instead of 2), no IF or PC-mux change
motivation:
The r7s2 ISS trace of the timed CoreMark window: 2,922,015 instructions,
4,442,763 cycles, 529,588 conditional branches (46,325 mispredicts on
the 64 x 2 agree-BHT), 49,367 JAL (all zero-bubble predicted in IF) and
13,735 JALR, every one a `ret` (jalr x0, 0(x1)). Every JALR goes through
fire_u and pays 2 bubbles (the entry squashed in EX by redirect_q plus
the one flushed in ID), i.e. ~27.5K cycles (0.62%).
LESSONS rule out every predictor structure tried so far: anything that
adds a leg, a select or a level to the IF next-PC cone or the PC mux
(r7s2 RAS -14%, r5s2 -9.5%, r9s0/r9s2 post-edge redirect logic), any BHT

cycle earlier, through the same redirect_q / redirect_tgt_q flops, with
no verification logic in EX (nothing is speculative, so no compare on

beyond one OR input). Epilogues restore ra at distance >= 2 from `ret`

most rets qualify.

the 4.6% bar on IPC (all ~60K redirects are ~2.7% of cycles), so this
slot is the predictor angle with the smallest possible timing footprint:
both PC-mux sources stay single flops and the IF stage is untouched.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
1. ID (id_stage.sv): decode, from the raw fetch word, jr_id = JALR
   opcode (1100111) && funct3 == 0 && imm[11:0] (fetch_word[31:20]) == 0
   && rd == x0 (ret form; drop the rd check only if it costs nothing),
   and jr_ok = jr_id && f1_r (sel_rf of rs1: no writer of rs1 in ID/EX
   or EX/MEM) && !rs1_data[1] (a misaligned target keeps the EX trap
   path). Export jr_fire_d = in.valid && jr_ok to ex_stage together with
   rs1_data. Register jr_ok into a new id_ex_t bit `jr_done`.
2. Gating of jr_fire_d (all early or already-present signals): ID/EX
   must capture this ret this cycle (!stall_id, !flush_id i.e. no
   load-use, no dmem/m stall, !redirect_q), and EX must not hold a
   control transfer that could itself fire (ex_ctl = in.valid &&
   (is_branch || is_jump) && !kill_q). A ret behind a branch in EX just
   falls back to the normal EX redirect (rare).
3. EX (ex_stage.sv): redirect_q D = redirect_fire | jr_fire_d (one more
   input on the existing final fire LUT; keep branch_cond as the last,
   latest input). Split the squash off redirect_q: new flop kill_q D =
   redirect_fire only; `kill`, fire_ok's !redirect_q, is_mop and the
   EX/MEM valid clear use kill_q (an ID-launched redirect must NOT kill
   the ret itself, which is in EX in the redirect cycle; only the
   wrong-path entry in ID is flushed, via flush_id on redirect_q as
   today). redirect_tgt_q D: keep the late AGU entering only the last
   LUT: final = jsel ? (agu[1] ? pc4 : {agu[31:1],0}) : other, where
   other = tgt_seq_early ? pc4 : ex_ctl ? branch_target : jr_rs1_data
   is precomputed from early/ID signals. fire_u excludes JALRs with
   in.jr_done (they already redirected). redirect_alt_q is only set by
   EX branches (unchanged). RVFI pc_next still comes from EX's agu
   (equal to rs1 for imm 0), so retirement fields are unchanged.
4. core.sv / hazard_unit.sv: wire rs1_data/jr_fire_d into ex_stage;
   flush_id stays (load_use || redirect_q) && !dmem_stall, which now
   also flushes the single wrong-path entry after an ID-launched
   redirect. The PC mux, if_stage.sv and the BHT are NOT touched.
   Corner case to test: unlike an EX-launched redirect, EX/MEM may hold
   a load/store in the ID-launched redirect cycle, so dmem_stall can be
   1 there; that is still correct (PC takes the target over the stall,
   ID/EX holds the ret, the wrong-path word in ID is never captured and
   ID/EX later captures the target word), but it must be covered.
Expected: cycles 4,442,763 -> ~4,430K (-0.25..-0.3%); Fmax unchanged
within noise only if the one extra OR input on redirect_q and the extra
precomputed leg on redirect_tgt_q stay off the last LUT. MUST record in
implementation_notes.md: the qualifying-ret count (sim), final cycle
count, LUT4/FF, and `python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options`
option-1 top-40 paths before and after. REVERT rule: if option-1 Fmax
drops > 1% vs 109.87 MHz, try (a) gating jr_fire_d with a registered
"ID/EX will capture" approximation instead of load_use, then (b) ship
the unchanged core and say so.
